text: This thing that you have done [is] not good. [As] the LORD lives, because you have not watched over your master, the LORD's anointed, you also are worthy to die. And now see where the king's spear [is], and the cruse of water that [was] at his head.

title: I Samuel 26:17
text: And Saul knew David's voice and said, [Is] this your voice, my son David? And David said, [It is] my voice, my lord, O king.

title: I Samuel 26:18
text: And he said, Why does my lord pursue after his servant this way? For what have I done? Or what evil [is] in my hand?

title: I Samuel 26:19
text: And now, please let my lord the king hear the words of his servant. If the LORD has stirred you up against me, let Him accept an offering. But if [it is] the sons of men, they [are] cursed before the LORD. For they have driven me out today from joining myself with the inheritance of the LORD, saying, Go, serve other gods.

title: I Samuel 26:20
text: And now, let not my blood fall to the earth before the face of the LORD. For the king of Israel has come out to seek a flea, as when one hunts a partridge in the mountains.

title: I Samuel 26:21
text: And Saul said, I have sinned. Return, my son David, for I will never do you harm any more, because my life was precious in your eyes this day. Behold, I have acted foolishly, and have greatly erred.

title: I Samuel 26:22
text: And David answered and said, Behold the king's spear! And let one of the young men come over and get it.

title: I Samuel 26:23
text: May the LORD give to each his righteousness and his faithfulness. For the LORD delivered you into [my] hand today, but I would not stretch forth my hand against the LORD's anointed.

title: I Samuel 26:24
text: And behold, as your life was precious in my eyes this day, so let my life be precious in the eyes of the LORD, and let Him deliver me out of all tribulation.

title: I Samuel 26:25
text: And Saul said to David, Blessed [are] you, my son David. You shall both do [great things] and also shall still prevail. So David went on his way, and Saul returned to his place.

title: I Samuel 27:1
text: And David said in his heart, I shall now perish one day by the hand of Saul. Nothing [is] better for me than that I should speedily escape into the land of the Philistines. And Saul shall despair of me, to seek me any more in any border of Israel, and so I shall escape out of his hand.

title: I Samuel 27:2
text: And David arose and passed over, he and the six hundred men with him to Achish the son of Maoch, king of Gath.

title: I Samuel 27:3
text: And David lived with Achish of Gath, he and his men, each one with his household; David with his two wives, Ahinoam of Jezreel, and Abigail of Carmel, Nabal's former wife.

title: I Samuel 27:4
text: And Saul was told that David had fled to Gath. And he never again looked for him.

title: I Samuel 27:5
text: And David said to Achish, If I have now found grace in your eyes, let them give me a place in some town in the country so that I may live there. For why should your servant live in the royal city with you?

title: I Samuel 27:6
text: And Achish gave him Ziklag that day. And Ziklag [belongs] to the kings of Judah to this day.

title: I Samuel 27:7
text: And the number of days that David lived in the field of the Philistines was [a year] of days and four months.

title: I Samuel 27:8
text: And David and his men went up and invaded the Geshurites, and the Gezrites, and the Amalekites. For they [were] the inhabitants of the land from the past [days], as you come into Shur, even into the land of Egypt.

title: I Samuel 27:9
text: And David struck the land, and did not keep alive man nor woman alive, and took away the sheep and the oxen and the asses and the camels and the clothing, and returned and came to Achish.

title: I Samuel 27:10
text: And Achish said, Where have you made a raid today? And David said, Against the south of Judah, and against the south of the Jerahmeelites, and against the south of the Kenites.

title: I Samuel 27:11
text: And David did not keep alive man or woman to bring [news] to Gath, saying, Lest they should tell on us, saying, So David did, and so [has been] his custom all the days he lived in the fields of the Philistines.

title: I Samuel 27:12
text: And Achish believed David, saying, He has made himself to be hated among his people Israel, and has become my servant forever.

title: I Samuel 28:1
text: And in those days it happened that the Philistines gathered their armies for war, to fight with Israel. And Achish said to David, You surely know that you shall go with me to battle, you and your men.

title: I Samuel 28:2
text: And David said to Achish, Surely you shall know what your servant can do. And Achish said to David, And I will make you keeper of my head forever.

title: I Samuel 28:3
text: And Samuel was dead, and all Israel had mourned him and buried him in Ramah, even in his own city. And Saul had put away those that had familiar spirits, and the wizards, out of the land.

title: I Samuel 28:4
text: And the Philistines gathered themselves and came and pitched in Shunem. And Saul gathered all Israel and they pitched in Gilboa.

title: I Samuel 28:5
text: And Saul saw the army of the Philistines, and he was afraid, and his heart greatly trembled.

title: I Samuel 28:6
text: And when Saul inquired of the LORD, the LORD did not answer him, neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets.

title: I Samuel 28:7
text: And Saul said to his servants, Seek me a woman who has a familiar spirit, so that I may go to her and inquire of her. And his servant said to him, Behold, [there is] a woman who is a necromancer at Endor.

title: I Samuel 28:8
text: And Saul disguised himself and put on other clothing. And he went. And two men went with him. And they came to the woman by night. And he said, Please divine for me [calling up the dead], and bring me up the man whom I shall name to you.

title: I Samuel 28:9
text: And the woman said to him, Behold, you know what Saul has done, how he has cut off those that have familiar spirits, and the wizards, out of the land. Why then do you lay a snare for my life, to cause me to die?

title: I Samuel 28:10
text: And Saul swore to her by the LORD, saying, [As] the LORD lives, there shall no punishment happen to you for this thing.

title: I Samuel 28:11
text: And the woman said, Whom shall I bring up to you? And he said, Bring me up Samuel.

title: I Samuel 28:12
text: And the woman saw Samuel, and cried with a loud voice. And the woman spoke to Saul, saying, Why have you deceived me? For you [are] Saul!

title: I Samuel 28:13
text: And the king said to her, Do not be afraid. For what did you see? And the woman said to Saul, I saw gods coming up out of the earth.

title: I Samuel 28:14
text: And he said to her, What [is] his form? And she said, An old man comes up, and he is covered with a cloak. And Saul saw that it was Samuel, and [he] bowed [his] face to the ground, and prostrated himself.

title: I Samuel 28:15
text: And Samuel said to Saul, Why have you disturbed me, to bring me up? And Saul answered, I am grievously distressed, for the Philistines are warring against me. And God has left me and does not answer me any more, neither by prophets nor by dreams. And I have called you so that you may make known to me what I should do.

title: I Samuel 28:16
text: And Samuel said, Why then do you ask me, since the LORD has left you and has become your enemy?

title: I Samuel 28:17
text: And the LORD has done for Himself as He spoke by me. For the LORD has torn the kingdom out of your hand and [is] giving it to your neighbor, to David.

title: I Samuel 28:18
text: Because you did not obey the voice of the LORD, nor execute his fierce wrath on Amalek, therefore the LORD has done this thing to you now.

title: I Samuel 28:19
text: And, the LORD will also deliver Israel with you into the hand of the Philistines. And tomorrow you and your sons [shall be] with me. The LORD also shall deliver the army of Israel into the hand of the Philistines.

title: I Samuel 28:20
text: And Saul immediately fell headlong on the earth, and was sorely afraid because of the words of Samuel. And there was no strength in him, for he had eaten no bread all day nor all night.

title: I Samuel 28:21
text: And the woman came to Saul and saw that he was sorely troubled, and said to him, Behold, your handmaid has obeyed your voice, and I have put my life in my hand, and have listened to your words which you spoke to me.

title: I Samuel 28:22
text: And now please listen also to the voice of your handmaid, and let me set a bit of bread before you and eat, so that you may have strength when you go on your way.

title: I Samuel 28:23
text: But he refused, and said, I will not eat. But his servants, forced him, and the woman also. And he listened to their voices and arose from the earth and sat on the bed.

title: I Samuel 28:24
text: And the woman had a fat calf in the house. And she hurried and killed it, and took flour and kneaded [it], and baked unleavened [bread] with it.

title: I Samuel 28:25
text: And [she] brought [it] before Saul, and before his servants. And they ate, and rose up and went away that night.

title: I Samuel 29:1
text: And the Philistines gathered all their armies to Aphek. And the Israelites pitched by a fountain in Jezreel.

title: I Samuel 29:2
text: And the lords of the Philistines passed on by hundreds and by thousands. But David and his men passed on in the rear with Achish.

title: I Samuel 29:3
text: And the rulers of the Philistines said, What [are] these Hebrews [doing]? And Achish said to the rulers of the Philistines, Is this not David the servant of Saul the king of Israel, who has been with me [these] days, or [ these] years. And I have not found anything [evil] in him from the day he fell away until today?

title: I Samuel 29:4
text: And the rulers of the Philistines were angry with him. And the Philistine rulers said to him, Send the man back, and he shall return to his place where you have appointed him. And he shall not go down with us to battle, and shall not become an enemy to us in battle. For with what should he reconcile himself to his master? [Should it] not [be] with the heads of these men?

title: I Samuel 29:5
text: [Is] not this David, of whom they sang to one another in dances, saying, Saul killed his thousands, and David his ten thousands?

title: I Samuel 29:6
text: And Achish called David and said to him, Surely, [as] the LORD lives, you have been upright, and your going out and your coming in with me in the army is good in my sight. For I have not found evil in you since the day of your coming to me until today. But you are not good in the eyes of the lords.

title: I Samuel 29:7
text: And return now, and go in peace so that you do not displease the lords of the Philistines.

title: I Samuel 29:8
text: And David said to Achish, But what have I done? And what have you found in your servant so long as I have been with you to this day, that I may not go fight against the enemies of my lord the king?

title: I Samuel 29:9
text: And Achish answered and said to David, I know that you [are] good in my sight, like an angel of God. But the princes of the Philistines have said, He shall not go up with us to the battle.

title: I Samuel 29:10
text: And now, rise up early in the morning with your master's servants who have come with you. And as soon as you have light, depart.

title: I Samuel 29:11
text: And David and his men rose up early to leave in the morning, to return into the land of the Philistines. And the Philistines went up [to] Jezreel.

title: I Samuel 30:1
text: And it happened when David and his men had come to Ziklag on the third day, the Amalekites had invaded the south and Ziklag, and had struck Ziklag, and burned it with fire.

title: I Samuel 30:2
text: And they had seized the women in it. They did not kill any, either small or great, but carried them away and went on their way.

title: I Samuel 30:3
text: And David and his men came to the city, and behold, [it was] burned with fire, and their wives and their sons and their daughters had been taken captives.

title: I Samuel 30:4
text: And David and the people with him lifted up their voice and wept, until they had no more power to weep.

title: I Samuel 30:5
text: And David's two wives had been seized, Ahinoam of Jezreel, and Abigail, the [former] wife of Nabal of Carmel.

title: I Samuel 30:6
text: And it greatly distressed David, for the people spoke of stoning him, because the soul of all the people was grieved, each one for his sons and for his daughters. But David encouraged himself in the LORD his God.

title: I Samuel 30:7
text: And David said to Abiathar the priest, Ahimelech's son, Please bring the ephod here to me. And Abiathar brought the ephod there to David.

title: I Samuel 30:8
text: And David inquired of the LORD, saying, Shall I go after this troop? Shall I overtake them? And He answered him, Go! For you shall surely overtake and will without fail recover all.

title: I Samuel 30:9
text: So David went, he and the six hundred men that [were] with him, and came to the brook Besor, where those who were left behind stayed.

title: I Samuel 30:10
text: But David pursued, he and four hundred men. For two hundred stayed behind, who were too exhausted to go over the brook Besor.

title: I Samuel 30:11
text: And they found an Egyptian in the field and brought him to David and gave him bread, and he ate. And they made him drink water.

title: I Samuel 30:12
text: And they gave him a piece of a cake of figs, and two clusters of raisins. And when he had eaten, his spirit came again to him. For he had eaten no bread nor drunk water for three days and three nights.

title: I Samuel 30:13
text: And David said to him, Whose [are] you? And where do you come from? And he said, I am an Egyptian youth, servant to an Amalekite. And my master left me because three days ago I fell sick.

title: I Samuel 30:14
text: We raided the south of the Cherethites, and on that [belonging] to Judah, and on the south of Caleb. And we burned Ziklag with fire.

title: I Samuel 30:15
text: And David said to him, Can you bring me down to this company? And he said, Swear to me by God that you will neither kill me nor deliver me into the hands of my master, and I will bring you down to this company.

title: I Samuel 30:16
text: And when he had brought him down, behold, [they were] spread abroad on all the earth, eating and drinking and dancing, because of all the great spoil that they had taken out of the land of the Philistines and out of the land of Judah.

title: I Samuel 30:17
text: And David struck them from the twilight even to the evening of the next day. And not a man of them escaped, except four hundred young men who rode on camels and fled.

title: I Samuel 30:18
text: And David recovered all that the Amalekites had carried away. And David rescued his two wives.

title: I Samuel 30:19
text: And nothing was lacking to them, from the small to the great, even to sons and daughters, and from the spoil, even to all that they had taken to themselves. David recovered all.

title: I Samuel 30:20
text: And David took all the flock, and the herd. They drove on before those cattle. And they said, This [is] David's spoil.

title: I Samuel 30:21
text: And David came to the two hundred who were too exhausted to follow David, whom they had made also to stay at the brook Besor. And they went out to meet David, and to meet the people with him. And David came up to the people, and greeted them.

title: I Samuel 30:22
text: And all the wicked men and [men] of Belial among the men who went with David answered and said, Because they did not go with us, we will not give them from a thing the spoil that we have seized, except to every man his wife and his sons. Let them take them, and go.

title: I Samuel 30:23
text: And David said, My brothers, you shall not do so with that which the LORD has given us. For He has protected us, and has delivered into our hand the company that came against us.

title: I Samuel 30:24
text: For who will listen to you in this matter? But as his part [is] that goes down to the battle, so [shall be] his part that stays by the stuff. They shall divide alike.

title: I Samuel 30:25
text: And it was [so], from that day forward he made it a statute and an ordinance for Israel to this day.

title: I Samuel 30:26
text: And David came to Ziklag, and sent some of the spoil to the elders of Judah, to his friends, saying, Behold, a present for you from the spoil of the enemies of the LORD;

title: I Samuel 30:27
text: to the ones in Bethel, and to the ones in Ramoth of the south, and to the ones in Jattir,

title: I Samuel 30:28
text: and to the ones in Aroer, and to the ones in Siphmoth, and to the ones in Eshtemoa,

title: I Samuel 30:29
text: and to the ones in Rachal, and to the ones in the cities of the Jerahmeelites, and to the ones in the cities of the Kenites,

title: I Samuel 30:30
text: and to the ones in Hormah, and to the ones in Chorashan, and to the ones in Athach,

title: I Samuel 30:31
text: and to the ones in Hebron, and to all the places where David had gone up and down, he and his men.

title: I Samuel 31:1
text: And the Philistines fought against Israel. And the men of Israel fled from before the Philistines, and fell down wounded in Mount Gilboa.

title: I Samuel 31:2
text: And the Philistines followed Saul and his sons. And the Philistines killed Jonathan and Abinadab and Malchishua, Saul's sons.

title: I Samuel 31:3
text: And the battle went hard against Saul. And the archers hit him, and he was sorely wounded by the archers.

title: I Samuel 31:4
text: And Saul said to his armor-bearer, Draw your sword and thrust me through with it, lest these uncircumcised ones come and thrust me through, and abuse me. But his armor-bearer would not, for he was very much afraid. So Saul took a sword and fell on it.

title: I Samuel 31:5
text: And when his armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he also fell on his sword and died with him.

title: I Samuel 31:6
text: And Saul died, and his three sons, and his armor-bearer, and all his men, that same day together.

title: I Samuel 31:7
text: And the men of Israel beyond the valley, and who [were] on the other side Jordan, saw that the men of Israel fled and that Saul and his sons had died. And they abandoned the cities and fled. And the Philistines came and lived in them.

title: I Samuel 31:8
text: And it happened on the next day, the Philistines came to strip the slain, and they found Saul and his three sons fallen in mount Gilboa.

title: I Samuel 31:9
text: And they cut off his head and stripped off his armor, and sent into the land of the Philistines all around, to publish [it] in the house of their idols and [among] the people.

title: I Samuel 31:10
text: And they put his armor in the house of Ashtaroth, and they fastened his body to the wall of Beth-shan.

title: I Samuel 31:11
text: And when they heard about it, the people of Jabesh-gilead, what the Philistines had done to Saul,

title: I Samuel 31:12
text: then all the brave men arose, and they traveled all night. And [they] took the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons from the wall of Beth-shan, and came to Jabesh, and burned them there.

title: I Samuel 31:13
text: And they took their bones and buried [them] under the tamarisk tree at Jabesh. And [they] fasted seven days.

title: II Samuel 1:1
text: And it happened after the death of Saul, David returned from the slaughter of the Amalekites, and David stayed two days in Ziklag,

title: II Samuel 1:2
text: on the third day, behold, a man came out of the camp from Saul with his clothes torn and earth upon his head. And it happened when he came to David, he fell to the earth and bowed to him.

title: II Samuel 1:3
text: And David said to him, Where do you come from? And he said to him, I have escaped out of the camp of Israel.

title: II Samuel 1:4
text: And David said to him, How did the matter go? Please tell me. And he answered, The people have fled from the battle, and many of the people also have fallen and are dead. And Saul and his son Jonathan are dead also.

title: II Samuel 1:5
text: And David said to the young man who told him, How do you know that Saul and his son Jonathan [are] dead?

title: II Samuel 1:6
text: And the young man who told him said, As I happened to be upon Mount Gilboa, behold, Saul leaned upon his spear. And, lo, the chariots and horsemen followed hard after him.

title: II Samuel 1:7
text: And when he looked behind him, he saw me, and called to me. And I answered, Here [am] I.

title: II Samuel 1:8
text: And he said to me, Who [are] you? And I answered him, I [am] an Amalekite.

title: II Samuel 1:9
text: He said to me again, Please stand over me and kill me, for anguish has come upon me, because all my life [is] still in me.

title: II Samuel 1:10
text: And I stood over him and killed him, because I was sure that he could not live after he had fallen. And I took the crown on his head, and [the] bracelet on his arm, and have brought them here to my lord.

title: II Samuel 1:11
text: And David took hold on his garments, and tore them. And likewise all the men with him [did] so.

title: II Samuel 1:12
text: And they mourned and wept and fasted until evening, for Saul, and for his son Jonathan, and for the people of the LORD, and for the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.

title: II Samuel 1:13
text: And David said to the young man who told him, From where [are] you? And he answered, I [am] the son of a stranger, an Amalekite.

title: II Samuel 1:14
text: And David said, Why were you not afraid to stretch forth your hand to destroy the LORD's anointed?

title: II Samuel 1:15
text: And David called one of the young men and said, Go near; fall on him. And he struck him so that he died.

title: II Samuel 1:16
text: And David said to him, Your blood [be] upon your head, for your mouth has testified against you, saying, I have slain the LORD's anointed.

title: II Samuel 1:17
text: And David chanted this death dirge over Saul and over his son Jonathan.

title: II Samuel 1:18
text: And he said to teach the sons of Judah [The Song of] the Bow. Behold, it is written in the Book of Jasher:

title: II Samuel 1:19
text: The beauty of Israel is slain upon your high places! How are the mighty fallen!

title: II Samuel 1:20
text: Tell [it] not in Gath, do not let it be known in the streets of Askelon, lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph.

title: II Samuel 1:21
text: Mountains of Gilboa, [let] not dew or rain [be] on you, nor fields of offerings. For there the shield of the mighty has been evilly cast away, the shield of Saul not [being] anointed with oil.

title: II Samuel 1:22
text: From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, the bow of Jonathan did not turn back, and the sword of Saul did not return empty.

title: II Samuel 1:23
text: Saul and Jonathan [were] lovely and pleasant in their lives, and in their death they were not divided. They were swifter than eagles; they were stronger than lions.

title: II Samuel 1:24
text: Daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, who clothed you in scarlet and with delights; who put ornaments of gold on your clothes.

title: II Samuel 1:25
text: How [are] the mighty fallen in the midst of the battle! Jonathan is slain on your high places.

title: II Samuel 1:26
text: I [am] distressed for you, my brother Jonathan. Very pleasant you have been to me. Your love to me was wonderful, more than the love of women.

title: II Samuel 1:27
text: How [are] the mighty fallen, and the weapons of war perished!

title: II Samuel 2:1
text: And it happened after this, David inquired of the LORD, saying, Shall I go up into any of the cities of Judah? And the LORD said to him, Go up! And David said, Where shall I go? And He said, To Hebron.

title: II Samuel 2:2
text: And David went up there, and his two wives also, Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail of Carmel, Nabal's wife.

title: II Samuel 2:3
text: And David brought up his men with him, each man with his household. And they lived in the cities of Hebron.

title: II Samuel 2:4
text: And the men of Judah came, and they anointed David king over the house of Judah there. And they told David, saying, The men of Jabesh-gilead buried Saul.

title: II Samuel 2:5
text: And David sent messengers to the men of Jabesh-gilead. And he said to them, Blessed [are] you of the LORD, that you have shown this kindness to your lord, to Saul, and have buried him.

title: II Samuel 2:6
text: And now may the LORD do kindness and truth to you. And I also do good to you, because you have done this thing.

title: II Samuel 2:7
text: And now let your hands be strengthened, and be brave. For your master Saul [is] dead, and also the house of Judah has anointed me king over them.

title: II Samuel 2:8
text: But Abner the son of Ner, commander of Saul's army, took Ishbosheth the son of Saul, and brought him over to Mahanaim.

title: II Samuel 2:9
text: And [he] made him king over Gilead, and over the Ashurites, and over Jezreel, and over Ephraim, and over Benjamin, and over all Israel.

title: II Samuel 2:10
text: Ishbosheth, Saul's son, [was] forty years old when he began to reign over Israel, and reigned two years. But the house of Judah followed David.

title: II Samuel 2:11
text: And it happened, the number of days that David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah was seven years and six months.

title: II Samuel 2:12
text: And Abner the son of Ner, and the servants of Ishbosheth the son of Saul, went out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.

title: II Samuel 2:13
text: And Joab the son of Zeruiah, and the servants of David, went out and met by the pool of Gibeon and sat down, the one on the one [side] of the pool, and the other on the other [side] of the pool.

title: II Samuel 2:14
text: And Abner said to Joab, Let the young men now arise and play before us. And Joab said, Let them arise.

title: II Samuel 2:15
text: And they arose and went over by number, twelve for Benjamin, and for Ishbosheth the son of Saul; and twelve of the servants of David.

title: II Samuel 2:16
text: And each one lay hold on the head, of his companion and [thrust] his sword in his companion's side, so that they fell together. And [one] called that place The Field of Rocks, which is in Gibeon.

title: II Samuel 2:17
text: And there was a very grievous battle that day. And Abner and the men of Israel were beaten before the servants of David.

title: II Samuel 2:18
text: And there were three sons of Zeruiah there, Joab and Abishai and Asahel. And Asahel [was] swift with his feet, like one of the gazelles in the field.

title: II Samuel 2:19
text: And Asahel ran after Abner, and in going he did not turn to the right hand nor to the left from following Abner.

title: II Samuel 2:20
text: And Abner looked behind him and said, [Are] you Asahel? And he answered, I [am].

title: II Samuel 2:21
text: And Abner said to him, Turn aside to your right hand or to your left, and lay hold on one of the young men, and take for yourself. But Asahel would not turn aside from following him.

title: II Samuel 2:22
text: And Abner said again to Asahel, Turn aside from following me. Why should I strike you to the ground? How then should I hold up my face to Joab your brother?

title: II Samuel 2:23
text: However he refused to turn aside. Therefore Abner struck him with the blunt end of the spear in the belly, and the spear came out behind him. And he fell down there, and died in the same place. And it happened that everyone who came to the place where Asahel fell down and died, stood still.

title: II Samuel 2:24
text: And Joab and Abishai ran after Abner. And the sun went down when they had come to the hill of Ammah, which [lies] before Giah by the way of the wilderness of Gibeon.

title: II Samuel 2:25
text: And the sons of Benjamin gathered themselves together after Abner, and became one troop, and stood on the top of a hill.

title: II Samuel 2:26
text: Then Abner called to Joab and said, Shall the sword devour forever? Do you not know that it will be bitter in the end? How long shall it be then before you command the people to return from chasing their brothers?

title: II Samuel 2:27
text: And Joab said, [As] God lives, unless you had spoken, surely then in the morning the people would have gone up each one from following his brother.

title: II Samuel 2:28
text: And Joab blew a ram's horn, and all the people stood still and did not pursue after Israel any more, nor did they fight any more.

title: II Samuel 2:29
text: And Abner and his men went all that night through the plain and passed over Jordan, and went all the forenoon and came to Mahanaim.

title: II Samuel 2:30
text: And Joab returned from following Abner. And when [he] had gathered all the people together, nineteen men and Asahel were missing from David's servants.

title: II Samuel 2:31
text: But the servants of David had stricken three hundred and sixty men of Benjamin, and of Abner's men, who died.

title: II Samuel 2:32
text: And they took up Asahel and buried him in the tomb of his father, which [was in] Bethlehem. And Joab and his men went all night, and they came to Hebron at the break of day.

title: II Samuel 3:1
text: And there was a long war between the house of Saul and the house of David. But David [became] stronger and stronger, and the house of Saul became weaker and weaker.

title: II Samuel 3:2
text: And sons were born to David in Hebron. And his first-born [was] Amnon, [the son of] Ahinoam of Jezreel.

title: II Samuel 3:3
text: And his second was Chileab, of Abigail of Carmel, the former wife of Nabal. And the third [was] Absalom, the son of Maacah the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur.

title: II Samuel 3:4
text: And the fourth [was] Adonijah, the son of Haggith. And the fifth [was] Shephatiah, the son of Abital.

title: II Samuel 3:5
text: And the sixth [was] Ithream, by Eglah, David's wife. These were born to David in Hebron.

title: II Samuel 3:6
text: And it happened, while there was war between the house of Saul and the house of David, Abner made himself strong for the house of Saul.

title: II Samuel 3:7
text: And Saul had a concubine whose name [was] Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah. And [Ishbosheth] said to Abner, Why have you gone in to my father's concubine?

title: II Samuel 3:8
text: And Abner was very angry over the words of Ishbosheth, and said, [Am] I a dog's head, who shows kindness against Judah this day to the house of Saul your father, to his brothers, and to his friends, and have not delivered you into the hand of David? [Am] I a dog's head that you charge me today with a fault concerning this woman today?

title: II Samuel 3:9
text: So may God do to Abner, and more also, if I do not do to David as the LORD has sworn,

title: II Samuel 3:10
text: to transfer the kingdom from the house of Saul, and to set up the throne of David over Israel and over Judah, from Dan even to Beer-sheba.

title: II Samuel 3:11
text: And he could not answer Abner a word again, because he feared him.

title: II Samuel 3:12
text: And Abner sent messengers to David on his behalf, saying, Whose [is] the land? He said, Cut your covenant with me, and, behold, my hand [shall be] with you, to bring about all Israel to you.

title: II Samuel 3:13
text: And he said, Good! I will cut a covenant with you, but one thing I ask of you, saying, You shall not see my face unless you first bring Michal, Saul's daughter, when you come to see my face.

title: II Samuel 3:14
text: And David sent messengers to Ishbosheth, Saul's son, saying, Deliver my wife Michal, whom I betrothed to me for a hundred foreskins of the Philistines.

title: II Samuel 3:15
text: And Ishbosheth sent and took her from [her] husband, from Phaltiel the son of Laish.

title: II Samuel 3:16
text: And her husband went along with her, weeping behind her, to Bahurim. And Abner said to him, Go, return! And he returned.

title: II Samuel 3:17
text: The word of Abner was with the elders of Israel, saying, You sought for David in times past [to be] king over you.

title: II Samuel 3:18
text: And then do [it], for the LORD has spoken of David, saying, By the hand of my servant David I will save My people Israel out of the hand of the Philistines, and out of the hand of all their enemies.

title: II Samuel 3:19
text: And Abner also spoke in the ears of Benjamin. And Abner went also to speak in the ears of David in Hebron all that seemed good to Israel, and all that seemed good to the whole house of Benjamin.

title: II Samuel 3:20
text: And Abner came to David at Hebron, and twenty men came with him. And David made a feast for Abner and the men who [were] with him.

title: II Samuel 3:21
text: And Abner said to David, I will arise and go, and will gather all Israel to my lord the king, so that they may make a covenant with you, and so that you may reign over all that your heart desires. And David sent Abner away, and he went in peace.

title: II Samuel 3:22
text: And behold, the servants of David and Joab came from [pursuing] a troop, and brought in a great spoil with them. But Abner [was] not with David in Hebron, for he had sent him away, and he had gone in peace.

title: II Samuel 3:23
text: And Joab and all the army with him came, and they told Joab, saying, Abner the son of Ner came to the king, and he has sent him away, and he has gone in peace.

title: II Samuel 3:24
text: And Joab came to the king and said, What have you done? Behold, Abner came to you. Why [is] this, [that] you have sent him away, and he has already gone?

title: II Samuel 3:25
text: You know Abner the son of Ner, that he came to deceive you, and to know your going out and your coming in, and to know all that you do.

title: II Samuel 3:26
text: And Joab left David and sent messengers after Abner, who brought him again from the well of Sirah. But David did not know.

title: II Samuel 3:27
text: And Abner returned to Hebron. And Joab took him aside in the gate to speak with him privately. And [he] struck him there in the belly, and he died, for the blood of Asahel his brother.

title: II Samuel 3:28
text: And afterward David heard, and said, My kingdom and I [are] guiltless before the LORD forever from the blood of Abner the son of Ner.

title: II Samuel 3:29
text: Let it whirl about the head of Joab, and on all his father's house. And let there not fail from the house of Joab one who has an issue, or who is a leper, or who leans on a staff, or who falls on the sword, or who lacks bread.

title: II Samuel 3:30
text: And Joab and Abishai his brother killed Abner, because he had slain their brother Asahel at Gibeon in the battle.

title: II Samuel 3:31
text: And David said to Joab and to all the people with him, Tear your clothes and gird yourselves with sackcloth, and mourn before Abner. And king David followed the bier.

title: II Samuel 3:32
text: And they buried Abner in Hebron. And the king lifted up his voice and wept at the grave of Abner. And all the people wept.

title: II Samuel 3:33
text: And the king mourned over Abner and said, Did Abner die like a fool dies?

title: II Samuel 3:34
text: Your hands [were] not bound, nor your feet put into fetters; as a man falls before wicked men, so you fell. And all the people wept again over him.

title: II Samuel 3:35
text: And all the people came to cause David to eat food while it was still day; David swore, saying, So let God do to me, and more also, if I taste bread or anything else until the sun is down.

title: II Samuel 3:36
text: And all the people took notice, and it pleased them, as whatever the king did pleased all the people.

title: II Samuel 3:37
text: For all the people and all Israel understood that day that it was not of the king to kill Abner the son of Ner.

title: II Samuel 3:38
text: And the king said to his servants, Do you not know that there is a prince and a great man fallen this day in Israel?

title: II Samuel 3:39
text: And I [am] weak this day, though anointed king. And these men, the sons of Zeruiah, [are] too hard for me. The LORD shall reward the doer of evil according to his wickedness.

title: II Samuel 4:1
text: And Saul's son heard that Abner was dead in Hebron. And his hands were feeble, and all the Israelites were troubled.

title: II Samuel 4:2
text: And Saul's son had two men [that were] captains of bands. The name of the one [was] Baanah, and the name of the other was Rechab, the sons of Rimmon of Beeroth, of the sons of Benjamin. For Beeroth also was counted to Benjamin;

title: II Samuel 4:3
text: and the men of Beeroth fled to Gittaim and were strangers there until this day.

title: II Samuel 4:4
text: And Jonathan, Saul's son, had a son who [was] lame in [his] feet. He was five years old when the news of Saul and Jonathan came out of Jezreel, and his nurse took him up and fled. And as she made haste to flee he fell and became lame. And his name [was] Mephibosheth.

title: II Samuel 4:5
text: And the sons of Rimmon of Beeroth, Rechab and Baanah, came at the heat of the day to the house of Ishbosheth. And he was lying [on his] bed [at] noon.

title: II Samuel 4:6
text: And they came to the midst of the house, bringing wheat. And they struck him in the belly. And Rechab and Baanah his brother escaped.

title: II Samuel 4:7
text: And they came into the house, and he lay in his bed in his bedroom. And they struck him and killed him, and beheaded him and took his head and got away through the plain all night.

title: II Samuel 4:8
text: And [they] brought the head of Ishbosheth to David at Hebron. and said to the king, Behold the head of Ishbosheth the son of Saul, your enemy who sought your life. And the LORD has avenged my lord the king this day of Saul and of his seed.

title: II Samuel 4:9
text: And David answered Rechab and Baanah his brother, the sons of Rimmon of Beeroth, and said to them, [As] the Lord lives, who has redeemed my soul out of all adversity,

title: II Samuel 4:10
text: when one told me, saying, Behold, Saul is dead, [thinking] to have brought good news, I took hold of him and killed him in Ziklag. I gave that to him as a reward.

title: II Samuel 4:11
text: Indeed when wicked men have slain a righteous person in his own house upon his bed, shall I not therefore now require his blood of your hand, and take you away from the earth?

title: II Samuel 4:12
text: And David commanded his young men, and they killed them, and cut off their hands and their feet, and hanged [them] up over the pool in Hebron. But they took the head of Ishbosheth and buried it in the tomb of Abner in Hebron.

title: II Samuel 5:1
text: And all the tribes of Israel came to David, to Hebron, and spoke, saying, Behold, we [are] your bone and your flesh.

title: II Samuel 5:2
text: Also in time past, when Saul was king over us, you were he who led Israel out and brought them in. And the LORD said to you, You shall feed My people Israel, and you shall be a leader over Israel.

title: II Samuel 5:3
text: And all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron. And king David made a covenant with them in Hebron before the LORD. And they anointed David king over Israel.

title: II Samuel 5:4
text: David [was] thirty years old when he began to reign. He reigned forty years.

title: II Samuel 5:5
text: In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months, and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty-three years over all Israel and Judah.

title: II Samuel 5:6
text: And the king and his men went to Jerusalem to the Jebusites, the people of the land. And one spoke to David saying, You shall not come in here, except the blind and the lame will turn you away; also saying, David cannot come in here.

title: II Samuel 5:7
text: And David took the stronghold of Zion; it [is] the city of David.

title: II Samuel 5:8
text: And David said on that day, Anyone who strikes the Jebusite, let him go by the water-shaft and [take] the lame and the blind, the hated of David's soul. On account of this they say, The blind and the lame shall not come into the house.

title: II Samuel 5:9
text: And David lived in the fort, and called it [the] city of David. And David built all around, from Millo and inward.

title: II Samuel 5:10
text: And David went on and became great, and the LORD God of hosts [was] with him.

title: II Samuel 5:11
text: And Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers, and cedar trees, and carpenters, and masons to David. And they built David a house.

title: II Samuel 5:12
text: And David saw that the LORD had established him king over Israel, and that He had made his kingdom sure for His people Israel's sake.

title: II Samuel 5:13
text: And David took more concubines and wives out of Jerusalem, after he had come from Hebron. And there were still more sons and daughters born to David.

title: II Samuel 5:14
text: These [are] the names of those to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, and Shobab, and Nathan, and Solomon,

title: II Samuel 5:15
text: and Ibhar, and Elishua, and Nepheg, and Japhia,

title: II Samuel 5:16
text: and Elishama, and Eliada, and Eliphalet.

title: II Samuel 5:17
text: And the Philistines heard that they had anointed David king over Israel. And all the Philistines came up to seek David. And David heard, and went down to the stronghold.

title: II Samuel 5:18
text: And the Philistines came and spread themselves in the Valley of the Giants.

title: II Samuel 5:19
text: And David inquired of the LORD, saying, Shall I go up to the Philistines? Will You deliver them into my hand? And the LORD said to David, Go up! For I will surely deliver the Philistines into your hand.

title: II Samuel 5:20
text: And David came to Baal-perazim, and David struck them there, and said, The LORD has broken forth [on] my enemies before me, like the breaking forth of waters. Therefore he called the name of that place The Breaking of Baal.

title: II Samuel 5:21
text: And they left their images there, and David and his men took them away.

title: II Samuel 5:22
text: And the Philistines came up again and spread themselves in the Valley of the Giants.

title: II Samuel 5:23
text: And David inquired of the LORD, and He said, You shall not go up, [but] go around behind them and come upon them over across from the weeping trees.

title: II Samuel 5:24
text: And it shall be, when you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the weeping trees, then you shall strike. For then the LORD shall go out before you to strike the army of the Philistines.

title: II Samuel 5:25
text: And David did so, as the LORD had commanded him. And [he] struck the Philistines from Geba until you come to Gezer.

title: II Samuel 6:1
text: Again David gathered every chosen one in Israel, thirty thousand.

title: II Samuel 6:2
text: And David arose and went with all the people with him from beyond Baale of Judah, to bring up the ark of God from there, which [is] called [by] the Name, the Name of the LORD of hosts who dwells [above] the cherubs.

title: II Samuel 6:3
text: And they set the ark of God upon a new cart, and brought it out of the house of Abinadab in Gibeah. And Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, drove the new cart.

title: II Samuel 6:4
text: And they brought it out of the house of Abinadab at Gibeah, going with the ark of God. And Ahio went before the ark.

title: II Samuel 6:5
text: And David and all the house of Israel [were dancing] the LORD on all [instruments] of fir wood, with lyres and with harps, and with tambourines, and with sistra, and with cymbals.

title: II Samuel 6:6
text: And when they came to Nachon's threshing-floor, Uzzah reached out to the ark of God, and took hold of it; for the oxen stumbled.

title: II Samuel 6:7
text: And the anger of the LORD was kindled against Uzzah. And God struck him there for the error. And he died there by the ark of God.

title: II Samuel 6:8
text: And David was displeased because the LORD had broken forth upon Uzzah. And he called the name of the place The Break of Uzzah to this day.

title: II Samuel 6:9
text: And David was afraid of the LORD that day, and said, How shall the ark of the LORD come to me?

title: II Samuel 6:10
text: And David was not willing to bring the ark of the LORD to him into the city of David. But David carried it aside into the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.

title: II Samuel 6:11
text: And the ark of the LORD stayed in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite three months. And the LORD blessed Obed-edom and all his household.

title: II Samuel 6:12
text: And they told king David, saying, The LORD has blessed the house of Obed-edom, and all that [belongs] to him, because of the ark of God. And David went and brought up the ark of God from the house of Obed-edom into the city of David with gladness.

title: II Samuel 6:13
text: And it happened that when those who bore the ark of the LORD had gone six steps, he sacrificed oxen and fatlings.

title: II Samuel 6:14
text: And David danced before the LORD with all [his] might. And David [was] girded with a linen ephod.

title: II Samuel 6:15
text: And David and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of the LORD with shouting, and with the sound of the ram's horn.

title: II Samuel 6:16
text: And it happened [as] the ark of the LORD came to the city of David, Michal, Saul's daughter, looked through a window and saw king David leaping and dancing before the LORD. And she despised him in her heart.

title: II Samuel 6:17
text: And they brought in the ark of the LORD and set it in its place in the midst of the tent that David had pitched for it. And David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD.

title: II Samuel 6:18
text: And as soon as David had made an end of offering burnt offerings and peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD of hosts.

title: II Samuel 6:19
text: And he gave out among all the people, among all the multitude of Israel, to the women as well as men, to each one a cake of bread and one raisin-cake. And all the people departed, each one to his house.

title: II Samuel 6:20
text: And David returned to bless his household. And Michal the daughter of Saul came out to meet David and said, How glorious was the king of Israel today, who uncovered himself today in the eyes of the handmaids of his servants, as one of the vain fellows shamelessly uncovers himself!

title: II Samuel 6:21
text: And David said to Michal, [It was] before the LORD, who chose me before your father, and before all his house, to appoint me ruler over the people of the LORD, over Israel. And I danced before the LORD.

title: II Samuel 6:22
text: And I will be still lower than this, and will be base in my own sight. And of the handmaids of whom you have spoken, with them I shall be had in honor.

title: II Samuel 6:23
text: And Michal the daughter of Saul had no child to the day of her death.

title: II Samuel 7:1
text: And it happened when the king dwelt in his house, and when the LORD had given him rest round about from all his enemies,

title: II Samuel 7:2
text: the king said to Nathan the prophet, See now, I live in a house of cedar, but the ark of God dwells within curtains.

title: II Samuel 7:3
text: And Nathan said to the king, Go, do all that [is] in your heart, for the LORD [is] with you.

title: II Samuel 7:4
text: And that night the word of the LORD came to Nathan saying,

title: II Samuel 7:5
text: Go and tell My servant David, So says the LORD, Shall you build Me a house for My dwelling?

title: II Samuel 7:6
text: For I have not dwelt in a house since the day that I brought up the sons out of Egypt until this day, but have walked in a tent, even in a tabernacle.

title: II Samuel 7:7
text: In all [places] in which I have walked with all the sons of Israel, did I speak a word with any of the tribes of Israel, [those] I commanded to feed My people Israel, saying, Why do you not build Me a house of cedars?

title: II Samuel 7:8
text: And now so shall you say to My servant David, So says the LORD of hosts: I took you from the sheepcote, from following the sheep, to be ruler over My people, over Israel.

title: II Samuel 7:9
text: And I was with you wherever you went, and have cut off all your enemies out of your sight, and have made you a great name like the name of the great ones in the earth.

title: II Samuel 7:10
text: And I will appoint a place for My people Israel, and will plant them so that they may dwell in a place of their own, and move no more. Neither shall the sons of wickedness afflict them any more, as before.

title: II Samuel 7:11
text: And even from the time that I commanded judges [to be] over My people of Israel, so will I cause you to rest from all your enemies. Also the LORD tells you that He will make you a house.

title: II Samuel 7:12
text: And when your days [are] fulfilled, and you shall sleep with your fathers, I will set up your seed after you, who shall come out of your bowels. And I will make his kingdom sure.

title: II Samuel 7:13
text: He shall build a house for My name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.

title: II Samuel 7:14
text: I will be his Father, and he shall be My son. If he commits iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the sons of men.

title: II Samuel 7:15
text: But My mercy shall not leave him, as I took [it] from Saul, whom I put away before you.

title: II Samuel 7:16
text: And your house and your kingdom shall be made sure forever before you. Your throne [shall be] established forever.

title: II Samuel 7:17
text: According to all these words, and according to all this vision, so Nathan spoke to David.

title: II Samuel 7:18
text: Then king David went in and sat before the LORD. And he said, Who [am] I, O Lord Jehovah? And what [is] my house, that You have brought me here?

title: II Samuel 7:19
text: And this was yet a small thing in Your sight, O Lord God. But You have spoken also of Your servant's house for a great while to come. And [is] this the manner of men, O Lord God?

title: II Samuel 7:20
text: And what can David say more to You? For You, O Lord Jehovah, know Your servant.

title: II Samuel 7:21
text: For Your word's sake, and according to Your own heart, You have done all these great things to make Your servant know.

title: II Samuel 7:22
text: Therefore You are great, O LORD God. For there is none like You, neither is there any God besides You, according to all that we have heard with our ears.

title: II Samuel 7:23
text: And what one nation in the earth [is] like Your people, like Israel, whom God went to redeem for a people to Himself, and to make Him a name, and to do for You great things and terrible, for Your land, before Your people, whom You redeemed to You from Egypt, from the nations and their gods?

title: II Samuel 7:24
text: For You have confirmed to Yourself Your people Israel [to be] a people to You forever. And You, LORD, have become their God.

title: II Samuel 7:25
text: And now, O LORD God, the word that You have spoken concerning Your servant, and concerning his house: establish [it] forever, and do as You have said.

title: II Samuel 7:26
text: And let Your name be magnified forever, saying, The LORD of hosts [is] the God over Israel. And let the house of Your servant David be established before You.

title: II Samuel 7:27
text: For You, O LORD of hosts, God of Israel, have revealed to Your servant, saying, I will build you a house. Therefore Your servant has found in his heart to pray this prayer to You.

title: II Samuel 7:28
text: And now, O Lord Jehovah, You [are] that God, and Your words are true, and You have promised this goodness to Your servant.

title: II Samuel 7:29
text: Therefore, now, let it please You to bless the house of Your servant, to be forever before You. For You, O Lord GOD, have spoken. And with Your blessing let the house of Your servant be blessed forever.

title: II Samuel 8:1
text: And it happened afterward, David struck the Philistines and humbled them. And David took The Bridle of the Metropolis out of the hand of the Philistines.

title: II Samuel 8:2
text: And he struck Moab, and measured them with a line, casting them down to the ground. Even with two lines he measured to put to death, and with one full line to keep alive. And the Moabites became David's servants, bringing gifts.

title: II Samuel 8:3
text: David also struck Hadadezer, the son of Rehob, king of Zobah, as he went to recover his border at the river [Euphrates].

title: II Samuel 8:4
text: And David took from him seventeen hundred horsemen, and twenty thousand footmen. And David hamstrung all the chariot [horses] but kept enough of them for a hundred chariots.

title: II Samuel 8:5
text: And when the Syrians of Damascus came to rescue Hadadezer king of Zobah, David killed twenty-two thousand men of the Syrians.

title: II Samuel 8:6
text: And David put troops in Syria of Damascus. And the Syrians became servants to David, bringing gifts. And the LORD preserved David wherever he went.

title: II Samuel 8:7
text: And David took the shields of gold that were on the servants of Hadadezer, and brought them to Jerusalem.

title: II Samuel 8:8
text: And from Betah, and from Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, king David took very much bronze.

title: II Samuel 8:9
text: And Toi king of Hamath heard that David had struck all the army of Hadadezer.

title: II Samuel 8:10
text: Then Toi sent Joram his son to king David, to greet him and bless him, because he had fought against Hadadezer and had struck him. For Hadadezer had wars against Toi. And in his hand were silver articles, and golden articles, and bronze articles.

title: II Samuel 8:11
text: King David also dedicated them to the LORD, with the silver and gold that he had dedicated from all nations which he subdued:

title: II Samuel 8:12
text: of Syria, and of Moab, and of the sons of Ammon, and of the Philistines, and of Amalek, and of the spoil of Hadadezer, son of Rehob, king of Zobah.

title: II Samuel 8:13
text: And David made a name [for himself] when he returned from striking the Syrians in the Valley of Salt, eighteen thousand [men].

title: II Samuel 8:14
text: And he put garrisons in Edom. He put garrisons throughout all Edom, and all the men of Edom became David's servants. And the LORD preserved David wherever he went.

title: II Samuel 8:15
text: And David reigned over all Israel. And David did judgment and justice to all his people.

title: II Samuel 8:16
text: And Joab the son of Zeruiah [was] over the army. And Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud [was] recorder.

title: II Samuel 8:17
text: And Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, [were] the priests. And Seraiah [was] the scribe.

title: II Samuel 8:18
text: And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada [was over] both the Cherethites and the Pelethites. And David's sons were priests.

title: II Samuel 9:1
text: And David said, Is there still any that is left from the house of Saul, that I may show him kindness for Jonathan's sake?

title: II Samuel 9:2
text: And [there was] of the house of Saul a servant whose name [was] Ziba. And they called him to David, and the king said to him, [Are] you Ziba? And he said, Your servant.

title: II Samuel 9:3
text: And the king said, [is] there not still any of the house of Saul, so that I may show the kindness of God to him? And Ziba said to the king, Jonathan still has a son, [who is] lame in his feet.

title: II Samuel 9:4
text: And the king said to him, Where [is] he? And Ziba said to the king, Behold, he [is] in the house of Machir, the son of Ammiel, in Lodebar.

title: II Samuel 9:5
text: And king David sent and brought him out of the house of Machir the son of Ammiel, from Lodebar.

title: II Samuel 9:6
text: And Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, came to David, and fell on his face and bowed to him. And David said, Mephibosheth! And he answered, Behold your servant!

title: II Samuel 9:7
text: And David said to him, Do not fear, for I will surely show you kindness for Jonathan your father's sake, and will restore you all the land of Saul your father. And you shall eat bread at my table forever.

title: II Samuel 9:8
text: And he bowed himself and said, What [is] your servant, that you should look upon such a dead dog as I?

title: II Samuel 9:9
text: Then the king called to Ziba, Saul's servant, and said to him, I have given to your master's son all that [belonged] to Saul and to all his house.

title: II Samuel 9:10
text: And you shall till the land for him, you and your sons and your servants. And you shall bring in [the fruits] so that your master's son may have bread to eat. But Mephibosheth, your master's son, shall eat bread always at my table. And Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.

title: II Samuel 9:11
text: And Ziba said to the king, According to all that my lord the king has commanded his servant, so shall your servant do. And Mephibosheth [was] eating at my table like one of the king's sons.

title: II Samuel 9:12
text: And Mephibosheth had a young son, whose name [was] Micah. And all that lived in the house of Ziba [were] servants to Mephibosheth.

title: II Samuel 9:13
text: And Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem. For he always sat at the king's table. And he [was] lame in both his feet.

title: II Samuel 10:1
text: And it happened after this, the king of the sons of Ammon died, and his son Hanun reigned in his stead.

title: II Samuel 10:2
text: And David said, I will show kindness to Hanun the son of Nahash, as his father showed kindness to me. And David sent to comfort him for his father, by the hand of his servants. And David's servants came to the land of the sons of Ammon.

title: II Samuel 10:3
text: And the leaders of the sons of Ammon said to Hanun their lord, Do you think that David honors your father, that he has sent comforters to you? Has not David sent his servants to you to search the city, and to spy it out, and to overthrow it?

title: II Samuel 10:4
text: And Hanun took David's servants and shaved off half their beards, and cut off their garments in the middle, to their buttocks, and sent them away.

title: II Samuel 10:5
text: And they told David, and he sent to meet them, because the men were greatly ashamed. And the king said, Stay at Jericho until your beards are grown, and return.

title: II Samuel 10:6
text: And the sons of Ammon saw that they had begun to stink before David. And the sons of Ammon sent and hired the Syrians of Beth-rehob, and the Syrians of Zobah, twenty thousand footmen, and from king Maacah a thousand men, and from Ishtob twelve thousand men.

title: II Samuel 10:7
text: And David heard. And he sent Joab and all the army of the mighty men.

title: II Samuel 10:8
text: And the sons of Ammon came out and put the battle in order at the entering in of the gate. And the Syrians of Zobah, and of Rehob, and Ishtob, and Maacah, [were] by themselves in the field.

title: II Samuel 10:9
text: And Joab saw that the front of the battle was against him before and behind. And he chose from all the choice ones of Israel, and put [them] in order against the Syrians.

title: II Samuel 10:10
text: And the rest of the people he delivered into the hand of Abishai his brother, so that he might set in order against the sons of Ammon.

title: II Samuel 10:11
text: And he said, If the Syrians are too strong for me, then you shall help me. But if the sons of Ammon are too strong for you, then I will come and help you.

title: II Samuel 10:12
text: Be of good courage, and let us play the men for our people and for the cities of our God. And may the LORD do that which seems good to Him.

title: II Samuel 10:13
text: And Joab and the people with him drew near to the battle against the Syrians. And they fled before him.

title: II Samuel 10:14
text: And when the sons of Ammon saw that the Syrians had fled, then they fled also before Abishai, and entered into the city. And Joab returned from the sons of Ammon and came to Jerusalem.

title: II Samuel 10:15
text: And the Syrians saw that they were beaten before Israel, and they gathered together.

title: II Samuel 10:16
text: And Hadarezer sent and brought out the Syrians who [were] beyond the river. And they came to Helam. And Shobach the commander of the army of Hadarezer went before them.

title: II Samuel 10:17
text: And David was told. And he gathered all Israel and passed over Jordan, and came to Helam. And the Syrians set themselves in order to meet David and fought with him.

title: II Samuel 10:18
text: And the Syrians fled before Israel. And David killed [the men of] seven hundred chariots of the Syrians, and forty thousand horsemen, and struck Shobach the captain of their army, who died there.

title: II Samuel 10:19
text: And all the kings, the servants of Hadarezer, saw that they were beaten before Israel, and [they] made peace with Israel and served them. And the Syrians feared to help the sons of Ammon any more.

title: II Samuel 11:1
text: And it happened at the turn of the year, at the time kings go forth, David sent Joab, and his servants with him, and all Israel. And they destroyed the sons of Ammon and circled Rabbah. But David remained at Jerusalem.

title: II Samuel 11:2
text: And it happened one evening, David arose from his bed and walked on the roof of the king's house. And from the roof [he saw] a woman bathing. And the woman [was] very beautiful to look upon.

title: II Samuel 11:3
text: And David sent and asked about the woman. And [one] said, [Is] not this Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliam, the wife of Uriah the Hittite?

title: II Samuel 11:4
text: And David sent messengers and took her. And she came in to him, and he lay with her. And she had purified herself from her uncleanness. And she returned to her house.

title: II Samuel 11:5
text: And the woman conceived, and sent and told David, and said, I [am] with child.

title: II Samuel 11:6
text: And David sent to Joab, [saying], Send me Uriah the Hittite. And Joab sent Uriah to David.

title: II Samuel 11:7
text: And when Uriah had come to him, David asked how Joab did, and how the people did, and how the war went.

title: II Samuel 11:8
text: And David said to Uriah, Go down to your house and wash your feet. And Uriah left the king's house. And a gift from the king went out after him.

title: II Samuel 11:9
text: But Uriah slept at the door of the king's house with all the servants of his lord, and did not go down to his house.

title: II Samuel 11:10
text: And they told David, saying, Uriah did not go to his house. And David said to Uriah, Did you not come from a journey? Why have you not gone down to your house?

title: II Samuel 11:11
text: And Uriah said to David, The ark and Israel and Judah abide in tents. And my lord Joab, and the servants of my lord, are camped in the open fields. Shall I then go to my house to eat and to drink and to lie with my wife? [As] you live, and [as] your soul lives, I will not do this thing.

title: II Samuel 11:12
text: And David said to Uriah, Stay here today also, and tomorrow I will let you go. And Uriah stayed in Jerusalem that day and the next day.

title: II Samuel 11:13
text: And when David had called him, he ate and drank before him. And he made him drunk. And at evening he went out to lie on his bed with the servants of his lord, but he did not go down to his house.

title: II Samuel 11:14
text: And it happened in the morning, David wrote a letter to Joab and sent [it] by the hand of Uriah.

title: II Samuel 11:15
text: And he wrote in the letter, saying, Set Uriah in the forefront of the hottest battle, and draw back from him so that he may be stricken and die.

title: II Samuel 11:16
text: And it happened when Joab observed the city, he sent Uriah to a place where he knew brave men [were].

title: II Samuel 11:17
text: And the men of the city went out and fought with Joab. And [some] of the people of the servants of David fell. And Uriah the Hittite also died.

title: II Samuel 11:18
text: Then Joab sent and told David all the things concerning the war.

title: II Samuel 11:19
text: And [he] commanded the messenger saying, When you have made an end of telling the matters of the war to the king,

title: II Samuel 11:20
text: and if it be so that the king's wrath arise, and he say to you, Why did you approach so near to the city when you fought? Did you not know that they would shoot from the wall?

title: II Samuel 11:21
text: Who struck Abimelech the son of Jerub-besheth? Did not a woman cast a piece of a millstone upon him from the wall, so that he died in Thebez? Why did you go near the wall? And you shall say, Your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.

title: II Samuel 11:22
text: And the messenger departed, and came and told David all that Joab had sent him to [tell].

title: II Samuel 11:23
text: And the messenger said to David, Surely the men prevailed against us, and came out to us to the field, and we were upon them even to the entering of the gate.

title: II Samuel 11:24
text: And the shooters shot from off the wall upon your servants, and [some] of the king's servants are dead, and your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.

title: II Samuel 11:25
text: Then David said to the messenger, So you shall say to Joab, Do not let this thing displease you, for the sword devours one as well as another. Make your battle stronger against the city and overthrow it. And you encourage him.

title: II Samuel 11:26
text: And the wife of Uriah heard that Uriah her husband [was] dead, and mourned for her husband.

title: II Samuel 11:27
text: And when her mourning was past, David sent and brought her to his house, and she became his wife and bore him a son. But the thing that David had done was evil in the eyes of the LORD.

title: II Samuel 12:1
text: And the LORD sent Nathan to David. And he came to him and said to him, There were two men in one city, one rich and one poor.

title: II Samuel 12:2
text: [The] rich one had exceeding many flocks and herds,

title: II Samuel 12:3
text: but the poor one had nothing except one little ewe lamb which he had bought and nourished up. And it grew up together with him and with his sons. It ate of his own food and drank from his own cup, and lay in his bosom, and was to him like a daughter.

title: II Samuel 12:4
text: And there came a traveler to the rich man, and he spared to take of his own flock and of his own herd to dress for the traveler that had come to him. But he took the poor man's lamb and dressed it for the man who had come to him.

title: II Samuel 12:5
text: And David's anger was greatly kindled against the man. And he said to Nathan, [As] the Lord lives, the man who has done this shall surely die.

title: II Samuel 12:6
text: And he shall restore the lamb fourfold, because he did this thing, and because he had no pity.

title: II Samuel 12:7
text: And Nathan said to David, You [are] the man! So says the LORD God of Israel, I anointed you king over Israel, and I delivered you out of the hand of Saul.

title: II Samuel 12:8
text: And I gave you your master's house and your master's wives into your bosom, and gave you the house of Israel and of Judah. And if that [was] too little, I would have given to you such and such [things] besides.

title: II Samuel 12:9
text: Why have you despised the word of the LORD, to do evil in His sight? You have stricken Uriah the Hittite with the sword, and have taken his wife [to be] your wife, and have killed him with the sword of the sons of Ammon.

title: II Samuel 12:10
text: And therefore, the sword shall never depart from your house, because you have despised Me and have taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be your wife.

title: II Samuel 12:11
text: So says the LORD, Behold, I will raise up evil against you out of your own house, and I will take your wives before your eyes and give [them] to your neighbor. And he shall lie with your wives in the sight of this sun.

title: II Samuel 12:12
text: For you did [it] secretly, but I will do this thing before all Israel and before the sun.

title: II Samuel 12:13
text: And David said to Nathan, I have sinned against the LORD. And Nathan said to David, The LORD also has put away your sin; you shall not die.

title: II Samuel 12:14
text: Only, because by this deed you have given great occasion to the enemies of the LORD to blaspheme, this child born to you shall surely die.

title: II Samuel 12:15
text: And Nathan left to go to his house. And the LORD struck the child that Uriah's wife bore to David, and it was very sick.

title: II Samuel 12:16
text: And David prayed to God for the child. And David fasted, and went in and lay all night upon the earth.

title: II Samuel 12:17
text: And the elders of his house rose up toward to him, to raise him up from the earth. But he would not, neither did he eat bread with them.

title: II Samuel 12:18
text: And it happened on the seventh day, the child died. And the servants of David feared to tell him that the child was dead. For they said, Behold, while the child was still alive we spoke to him, and he would not listen to our voice. How then will he trouble himself if we tell him that the child is dead?

title: II Samuel 12:19
text: But David saw that his servants whispered. And David understood that the child was dead. And David said to his servants, Is the boy dead? And they said, He is dead.

title: II Samuel 12:20
text: And David arose from the earth and washed, and anointed [himself], and changed his clothing, and came into the house of the LORD and worshiped. And he came to his house, and commanded, and they brought bread before him and he ate.

title: II Samuel 12:21
text: Then his servants said to him, What [is] this that you have done? You fasted and wept for the living boy, but when the child was dead you arose and ate bread!

title: II Samuel 12:22
text: And he said, While the child was still alive, I fasted and wept; for I said, Who can tell [if] God will be gracious to me so that the child may live?

title: II Samuel 12:23
text: But now he is dead; why should I fast? Can I bring him back again? I shall go to him, but he shall not return to me.

title: II Samuel 12:24
text: And David comforted his wife Bathsheba. And he went in to her and lay with her. And she bore a son. And he called his name Solomon. And the LORD loved him.

title: II Samuel 12:25
text: And he sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet, and he called his name Jedidiah, because of Jehovah.

title: II Samuel 12:26
text: And Joab fought against Rabbah of the sons of Ammon, and took the royal city.

title: II Samuel 12:27
text: And Joab sent messengers to David and said, I have fought against Rabbah, and have taken the city of waters.

title: II Samuel 12:28
text: And therefore gather the rest of the people together, and camp against the city and take it, lest I take the city and it be called after my name.

title: II Samuel 12:29
text: And David gathered all the people and went to Rabbah, and fought against it and took it.

title: II Samuel 12:30
text: And he took the king's crown from off his head, the weight of which [was] a talent of gold, and a precious stone in it. And it was [set] on David's head. And he brought forth the spoil of the city in great abundance.

title: II Samuel 12:31
text: And he brought forth the people that [were] in it, and put them to the saw, and to sharp tools of iron, and to axes of iron. And he made them go over into the brick-kiln. And so he did to all the cities of the sons of Ammon. And David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.

title: II Samuel 13:1
text: And it happened after this Absalom the son of David had a beautiful sister whose name [was] Tamar. And Amnon the son of David loved her.

title: II Samuel 13:2
text: And Amnon was so troubled that he fell sick for his sister Tamar, for she [was] a virgin. And Amnon thought it hard for him to do anything to her.

title: II Samuel 13:3
text: And Amnon had a friend, whose name [was] Jonadab, the son of David's brother Shimeah. And Jonadab [was] a very crafty man.

title: II Samuel 13:4
text: And he said to him, Why [are] you, the king's son, lean from day to day? Will you not tell me? And Amnon said to him, I love Tamar, my brother Absalom's sister.

title: II Samuel 13:5
text: And Jonadab said to him, Lay down on your bed and make yourself sick. And when your father comes to see you, say to him, Please let my sister Tamar come and give me food, and prepare the food in my sight so that I may see and eat [it] at her hand.

title: II Samuel 13:6
text: And Amnon lay down and made himself sick. And when the king had come to see him, Amnon said to the king, Please let my sister Tamar come and make me a couple of cakes in my sight, so that I may eat at her hand.

title: II Samuel 13:7
text: And David sent home to Tamar, saying, Go now to your brother Amnon's house, and prepare food for him.

title: II Samuel 13:8
text: And Tamar went to her brother Amnon's house. And he had lain down. And she took flour and kneaded [it], and made cakes in his sight, and baked the cakes.

title: II Samuel 13:9
text: And she took a pan and poured [them] out before him. But he refused to eat. And Amnon said, Make every man go out from me. And every man went out from him.

title: II Samuel 13:10
text: And Amnon said to Tamar, Bring the food into the room so that I may eat out of your hand. And Tamar took the cakes which she had made, and brought [them] into the room to Amnon her brother.

title: II Samuel 13:11
text: And when she had brought [them] to him to eat, he took hold of her and said to her, Come lie with me, my sister.

title: II Samuel 13:12
text: And she answered him, No, my brother, do not humble me. For no such thing ought to be done in Israel. Do not do this folly.

title: II Samuel 13:13
text: And I, where shall I cause my shame to go? And as for you, you shall be as one of the fools in Israel. But now please speak to the king. For he will not withhold me from you.

title: II Samuel 13:14
text: But he would not listen to her voice; but being stronger than she, he forced her and lay with her.

title: II Samuel 13:15
text: Then Amnon hated her with a great hatred. And the hatred with which he hated her [was] greater than the love with which he had loved her. And Amnon said to her, Get up and go.

title: II Samuel 13:16
text: And she said to him, [There is] no cause. This evil in sending me away [is] greater than the other that you did to me. But he would not listen to her.

title: II Samuel 13:17
text: And he called his servant who waited on him and said, And put this [woman] out from me, and bolt the door after her.

title: II Samuel 13:18
text: And [she had] a robe of many colors upon her, for the king's virgin daughters were clothed with such robes. And his servant brought her out and bolted the door after her.

title: II Samuel 13:19
text: And Tamar put ashes on her head and tore the robe of many colors that [was] on her, and laid her hand on her head, and went on, crying.

title: II Samuel 13:20
text: And Absalom her brother said to her, Has Amnon your brother been with you? But now hold your peace, my sister. He [is] your brother. Do not set your heart on this thing. And Tamar remained desolate in the house of her brother Absalom.

title: II Samuel 13:21
text: And when king David heard of all these things, he was very angry.

title: II Samuel 13:22
text: And Absalom did not speak to his brother Amnon, neither good nor bad, for Absalom hated Amnon because he had forced his sister Tamar.

title: II Samuel 13:23
text: And it happened after two full years Absalom had sheepshearers in Baal-hazor, beside Ephraim. And Absalom invited all the king's sons.

title: II Samuel 13:24
text: And Absalom came to the king and said, Behold now, your servant has shearers. Please let the king and his servants go with your servant.

title: II Samuel 13:25
text: And the king said to Absalom, No, my son, let us not all go now, lest we be too heavy upon you. And he pressed him. He would not go, however, but blessed him.

title: II Samuel 13:26
text: Then Absalom said, If not, please let my brother Amnon go with us? And the king said to him, Why should he go with you?

title: II Samuel 13:27
text: But Absalom pressed him, so that he let Amnon and all the king's sons go with him.

title: II Samuel 13:28
text: And Absalom had commanded his servants, saying, And watch when Amnon's heart is merry with wine, and when I say to you, Strike Amnon, you shall kill him. Do not fear. Have I not commanded you? Be courageous, and be brave.

title: II Samuel 13:29
text: And the servants of Absalom did to Amnon as Absalom had commanded. And all the king's sons arose. And they each got on his mule and fled.

title: II Samuel 13:30
text: And it happened while they were in the way, news came to David, saying, Absalom has killed all the king's sons, and there is not one of them left.

title: II Samuel 13:31
text: And the king arose and tore his garments, and lay on the earth. And all his servants stood by with their clothes torn.

title: II Samuel 13:32
text: And Jonadab, the son of David's brother Shimeah answered and said, Let not my lord think that they have killed all the young men, the king's sons. For only Amnon is dead. For by the mouth of Absalom this has been determined from the day that he humbled his sister Tamar.

title: II Samuel 13:33
text: And now do not let my lord the king take the thing to his heart, to think that all the king's sons are dead, for only Amnon is dead.

title: II Samuel 13:34
text: But Absalom fled. And the young man that kept the watch lifted up his eyes and looked. And, behold, many people came by the way of the hillside behind him.

title: II Samuel 13:35
text: And Jonadab said to the king, Behold, the king's sons come; as your servant said, so it is.

title: II Samuel 13:36
text: And it happened as soon as he had made an end of speaking, behold, the king's sons came. And they lifted up their voice and wept. And the king also and all his servants wept with a great weeping.

title: II Samuel 13:37
text: But Absalom fled and went to Talmai, the son of Ammihud, king of Geshur. And [David] mourned for his son every day.

title: II Samuel 13:38
text: And Absalom fled and went to Geshur, and was there three years.

title: II Samuel 13:39
text: And king David longed to go forth to Absalom, for he was comforted about Amnon, since he was dead.

title: II Samuel 14:1
text: And Joab the son of Zeruiah saw that the king's heart [was] toward Absalom.

title: II Samuel 14:2
text: And Joab sent to Tekoah and brought a wise woman from there. And he said to her, Please pretend yourself to be a mourner, and put on mourning clothes now, and do not anoint yourself with oil. But be like a woman who has mourned for the dead a long time.

title: II Samuel 14:3
text: And come to the king, and speak in this way to him. And Joab put the words in her mouth.

title: II Samuel 14:4
text: And the woman of Tekoah spoke to the king, and bowed and said, Save, O, King!

title: II Samuel 14:5
text: And the king said to her. What ails you? And she answered, I [am] indeed a widow, and my husband died.

title: II Samuel 14:6
text: And your handmaid had two sons, and the two of them fought together in the field. And [there was] no deliverer between them, but the one struck the other and killed him.

title: II Samuel 14:7
text: And behold, the whole family has risen against your handmaid. And they said, Deliver him who struck his brother so that we may kill him for the life of his brother whom he killed. And we will destroy the heir also. And so they shall put out my coal which is left, and shall leave to my husband [neither] name nor remainder upon the face of the earth.
