title: II Samuel 14:8
text: And the king said to the woman, Go to your house, and I will give command concerning you.

title: II Samuel 14:9
text: And the woman of Tekoah said to the king. My lord, O king, may the iniquity [be] on me and on my father's house. And may the king and his throne [be] without guilt.

title: II Samuel 14:10
text: And the king said, Whoever speaks to you, you also bring him to me, and he shall not touch you any more.

title: II Samuel 14:11
text: Then she said, Please let the king remember the LORD your God, that you would not allow the avengers of blood to destroy any more, lest they should destroy my son. And he said, [As] the Lord lives, there shall not one hair of your son fall to the earth.

title: II Samuel 14:12
text: Then the woman said, Please let your handmaid speak [one] more word to my lord the king. And he said, Say on!

title: II Samuel 14:13
text: And the woman said, Why then have you thought such a thing against the people of God? For the king speaks this thing as one who is at fault, in that the king does not bring his banished one home again.

title: II Samuel 14:14
text: For we must all die, and we [are] as water spilled on the ground, which cannot be gathered up again. And God does not take a life, but has devised plans so that the outcast is not cast out from Him.

title: II Samuel 14:15
text: And now I have come to speak of this thing to my lord the king, because the people have made me afraid. And your handmaid said, I will now speak to the king. It may be that the king will do what his handmaid has asked.

title: II Samuel 14:16
text: For the king will hear, to deliver his handmaid out of the hand of the man [who would] destroy me and my son together out of the inheritance of God.

title: II Samuel 14:17
text: And your handmaid said, The word of my lord the king shall now be comforting. For as an angel of God, so [is] my lord the king, to see what is good and bad. And the LORD your God will be with you.

title: II Samuel 14:18
text: And the king answered and said to the woman, Please do not hide from me the thing that I shall ask you. And the woman said, Let my lord the king now speak.

title: II Samuel 14:19
text: And the king said, [Is] the hand of Joab with you in all this? And the woman answered and said, [As] your soul lives, my lord the king, none shall turn to the right hand or to the left from anything which my lord the king has spoken. For your servant Joab commanded me. And he put all these words in the mouth of your handmaid.

title: II Samuel 14:20
text: Your servant Joab has done this thing to change the face of the matter. And my lord [is] wise according to the wisdom of an angel of God, to know all that is in the land.

title: II Samuel 14:21
text: And the king said to Joab, Behold now, I have done this thing. Go therefore and bring the young man Absalom again.

title: II Samuel 14:22
text: And Joab fell to the ground on his face, and bowed himself, and thanked the king. And Joab said, Today your servant knows that I have found grace in your sight, my lord, O, king, in that the king has done what your servant has asked.

title: II Samuel 14:23
text: And Joab arose and went to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.

title: II Samuel 14:24
text: And the king said, Let him turn to his own house, and let him not see my face. And Absalom returned to his own house, and did not see the king's face.

title: II Samuel 14:25
text: But in all Israel there was not a man handsome like Absalom. From the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him.

title: II Samuel 14:26
text: And when he sheared his head (for it was at every year's end that he sheared it, because it was heavy on him. And he sheared it), and he weighed the hair of his head at two hundred shekels, according to the king's weight.

title: II Samuel 14:27
text: And there were born three sons to Absalom, and one daughter, whose name [was] Tamar. She was a woman with a beautiful face.

title: II Samuel 14:28
text: And Absalom lived two full years in Jerusalem and did not see the king's face.

title: II Samuel 14:29
text: And Absalom sent to Joab, to send him to the king. But he would not come to him. And when he sent again a second time, he would not come.

title: II Samuel 14:30
text: And he said to his servants, See, Joab's field is near mine, and he has barley there. Go and set it on fire! And Absalom's servants set the field on fire.

title: II Samuel 14:31
text: And Joab arose and came to Absalom's house, and said to him, Why have your servants set my field on fire?

title: II Samuel 14:32
text: And Absalom answered Joab, Behold, I sent to you, saying, Come here so that I may send you to the king, to say, Why [have] I come from Geshur? It [was] good for me to be there still. And now let me see the king's face, and if there is iniquity in me, let him kill me.

title: II Samuel 14:33
text: And Joab came to the king and told him. And when he had called for Absalom, he came to the king and bowed himself on his face to the ground before the king. And the king kissed Absalom.

title: II Samuel 15:1
text: And it happened after this, Absalom prepared himself chariots and horses and fifty men to run before him.

title: II Samuel 15:2
text: And Absalom rose up early and stood beside the way of the gate. And it was [so], if any man had a suit to come before the king for judgment, then Absalom called to him and said, What city [are] you from? And he said, Your servant is of one of the tribes of Israel.

title: II Samuel 15:3
text: And Absalom said to him, See! Your matters [are] good and right. But no listener from the king [will hear] you.

title: II Samuel 15:4
text: And Absalom said, Oh that I might be made judge in the land, so that every man who has any suit or cause might come to me, and I would do him justice!

title: II Samuel 15:5
text: And it was [so], when any man came near to bow down to him, he put forth his hand and took him and kissed him.

title: II Samuel 15:6
text: And in this way Absalom did to all Israel that came to the king for judgment. And Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.

title: II Samuel 15:7
text: And it happened at the end of forty years, Absalom said to the king, Please let me go and pay my vow which I have vowed to the LORD in Hebron.

title: II Samuel 15:8
text: For your servant vowed a vow while I lived at Geshur in Syria, saying, If the LORD will indeed bring me again to Jerusalem, then I will serve the LORD.

title: II Samuel 15:9
text: And the king said to him, Go in peace. And he arose and went to Hebron.

title: II Samuel 15:10
text: But Absalom sent spies throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, As soon as you hear the sound of the ram's horn, then you shall say, Absalom reigns in Hebron!

title: II Samuel 15:11
text: And with Absalom went two hundred called men out of Jerusalem. And they went in their honesty, and did not know anything.

title: II Samuel 15:12
text: And Absalom sent for Ahithophel of Giloh, David's counselor, from his city Giloh, while he offered sacrifices. And the conspiracy was strong, for the people with Absalom grew more and more.

title: II Samuel 15:13
text: And a messenger came to David saying, The hearts of the men of Israel are after Absalom.

title: II Samuel 15:14
text: And David said to all his servants with him at Jerusalem, Arise, and let us flee! For [otherwise] we shall not escape from Absalom. Make haste to depart, lest he overtake us suddenly and bring evil upon us, and strike the city with the edge of the sword.

title: II Samuel 15:15
text: And the king's servants said to the king, Behold. your servants [will do] whatever my lord the king shall choose.

title: II Samuel 15:16
text: And the king went forth, and all his household after him. And the king left ten women, concubines, to keep the house.

title: II Samuel 15:17
text: And the king went forth, and all the people after him, and stayed in a place that was far off.

title: II Samuel 15:18
text: And all his servants passed on beside him. And all the Cherethites, and all the Pelethites, and all the Gittites, six hundred men who came after him from Gath, passed on before the king.

title: II Samuel 15:19
text: Then the king said to Ittai the Gittite, Why do you also go with us? Return to your place, and stay with the king. For you [are] a stranger, and also an exile.

title: II Samuel 15:20
text: Since you came [only] yesterday, should I make you go up and down with us today? Since I go where I may, you may return and take back your brothers. May mercy and truth be with you.

title: II Samuel 15:21
text: And Ittai answered the king and said, [As] the Lord lives, and [as] my lord the king lives, surely in whatever place my lord the king shall be, whether in death or life, even there also will your servant be.

title: II Samuel 15:22
text: And David said to Ittai, Go and pass over. And Ittai the Gittite passed over, and all his men, and all the little ones with him.

title: II Samuel 15:23
text: And all the country wept [with] a loud voice, and all the people passed over. The king himself also passed over the brook Kidron, and all the people passed over toward the way of the wilderness.

title: II Samuel 15:24
text: And lo, Zadok came also, and all the Levites [were] with him, carrying the ark of the covenant of God. And they set down the ark of God. And Abiathar went up until all the people had finished passing out of the city.

title: II Samuel 15:25
text: And the king said to Zadok, Carry the ark of God back into the city. If I shall find favor in the eyes of the LORD, He will bring me again and show it to me, and its dwelling place also.

title: II Samuel 15:26
text: But if He says this, I have no delight in you; behold me, and let Him do to me as [seems] good to Him.

title: II Samuel 15:27
text: The king also said to Zadok the priest, [Are] you a seer? Return to the city in peace, and your two sons with you. Ahimaaz your son, and Jonathan the son of Abiathar.

title: II Samuel 15:28
text: Behold, I will wait in the plain of the wilderness until there comes word from you to tell me.

title: II Samuel 15:29
text: And Zadok and Abiathar carried the ark of God again to Jerusalem. And they remained there.

title: II Samuel 15:30
text: And David went up by the ascent of [mount] Olivet. And he wept as he went up, and had his head covered, and he went barefoot. And of all the people with him, each man covered his head. And they went up, weeping as they went.

title: II Samuel 15:31
text: And [one] told David, saying, Ahithophel [is] among the conspirators with Absalom. And David said, O LORD, I pray You, turn the advice of Ahithophel to foolishness.

title: II Samuel 15:32
text: And it happened [when] David had come to the top, where he worshiped God, behold, Hushai the Archite came to meet him with his coat torn and earth upon his head.

title: II Samuel 15:33
text: David said to him, If you pass on with me, then you shall be a burden to me.

title: II Samuel 15:34
text: But if you return to the city and say to Absalom, I [will be] your servant, O king; I have been your father's servant until now, and now I also [will be] your servant, then you may break down the advice of Ahithophel for me.

title: II Samuel 15:35
text: And [do you] not [have] there with you Zadok and Abiathar the priests? And it shall be, whatever you shall hear out of the king's house, you shall tell it to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.

title: II Samuel 15:36
text: Behold, [they have] their two sons there with them, Ahimaaz, Zadok's son, and Jonathan, Ahimaaz's son. And you shall send to me everything that you hear by them.

title: II Samuel 15:37
text: And David's friend Hushai came to the city. And Absalom came into Jerusalem.

title: II Samuel 16:1
text: And David had passed on a little from the top. And, behold, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth met [him] with a couple of asses saddled, and upon them two hundred [loaves] of bread, and a hundred bunches of raisins, and a hundred of summer fruits, and a bottle of wine.

title: II Samuel 16:2
text: And the king said to Ziba, What are these to you? And Ziba said, The asses [are] for the king's household to ride upon. And the bread and summer fruit are for the young men to eat. And the wine is so that the ones who are faint in the wilderness may drink.

title: II Samuel 16:3
text: And the king said, And where [is] your master's son? And Ziba said to the king, Behold, he remains at Jerusalem. For he said, Today the house of Israel shall restore to me the kingdom of my father.

title: II Samuel 16:4
text: And the king said to Ziba, Behold, All that [belonged] to Mephibosheth [is] yours. And Ziba said, I humbly beg you that I may find grace in your sight, my lord, O king.

title: II Samuel 16:5
text: And king David came to Bahurim. And, behold, a man of the house of Saul came out from there, whose name [was] Shimei, the son of Gera. He came out, and he came cursing.

title: II Samuel 16:6
text: And he threw stones at David and at all the servants of king David. And all the people and all the mighty men [were] on his right hand, and on his left.

title: II Samuel 16:7
text: And Shimei said this in his cursing, Go out, O man of blood, O man of Belial.

title: II Samuel 16:8
text: The LORD has returned on you all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose place you have reigned. And the LORD has delivered the kingdom into the hand of Absalom your son. And behold, you [are] [taken] in your mischief, because you [are] a man of blood!

title: II Samuel 16:9
text: And Abishai the son of Zeruiah said to the king, Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Please let me go over and take off his head.

title: II Samuel 16:10
text: And the king said, What have I to do with you, sons of Zeruiah? Let him curse, because the LORD has said to him, Curse David. Who then shall say, Why have you done so?

title: II Samuel 16:11
text: And David said to Abishai and to all his servants, Behold, my son, who came forth from my bowels, seeks my life; and surely now [this] Benjamite? Let him alone and let him curse, for the LORD has spoken to him.

title: II Samuel 16:12
text: It may be that the LORD will look on my affliction, and that the LORD will repay me with good for his cursing this day.

title: II Samuel 16:13
text: And David and his men went by the highway. And Shimei went along on the hillside over across from him, and cursed [as] he went, and threw stones at him, and threw dust.

title: II Samuel 16:14
text: And the king, and all the people with him arrived weary. And they refreshed themselves there.

title: II Samuel 16:15
text: And Absalom and all the people, the men of Israel, came to Jerusalem. And Ahithophel went with him.

title: II Samuel 16:16
text: And it happened, when Hushai the Archite, David's friend, had come to Absalom, Hushai said to Absalom, Let the king live, let the king live!

title: II Samuel 16:17
text: And Absalom said to Hushai, [Is] this your kindness to your friend? Why did you not go with your friend?

title: II Samuel 16:18
text: And Hushai said to Absalom, No, but whom the LORD and this people, and all the men of Israel choose, his will I be, and I will stay with him.

title: II Samuel 16:19
text: And again, whom should I serve? [Should I] not serve in the presence of his son? As I have served in your father's presence, so I will be in your presence.

title: II Samuel 16:20
text: And Absalom said to Ahithophel, Give your advice. What shall we do?

title: II Samuel 16:21
text: And Ahithophel said to Absalom, Go in to your father's concubines, that he left to keep the house. And all Israel shall hear that you are abhorred by your father. And the hands of all who [are] with you will be strong.

title: II Samuel 16:22
text: And they spread Absalom a tent on the top of the house, and Absalom went in to his father's concubines in the sight of all Israel.

title: II Samuel 16:23
text: And the advice of Ahithophel, which he advised in those days, [was] as if a man had inquired at the oracle of God. So [was] all the advice of Ahithophel, both with David and with Absalom.

title: II Samuel 17:1
text: And Ahithophel said to Absalom, Please let me choose out twelve thousand men, and I will arise and pursue after David tonight.

title: II Samuel 17:2
text: And I will come upon him while he [is] weary and weak-handed, and I will make him tremble. And all the people with him will flee. And I will strike the king by himself.

title: II Samuel 17:3
text: And I will bring back all the people to you, when all return, except the man whom you [are] seeking. All the people shall be in peace.

title: II Samuel 17:4
text: And the saying pleased Absalom very much, and all the elders of Israel.

title: II Samuel 17:5
text: And Absalom said, Please call Hushai the Archite also, and let us hear likewise what is in his mouth.

title: II Samuel 17:6
text: And Hushai came in to Absalom. And Absalom spoke to him saying, Ahithophel has spoken in this way. Shall we do his word? If not, you speak.

title: II Samuel 17:7
text: And Hushai said to Absalom, The advice which Ahithophel has given [is] not good at this time.

title: II Samuel 17:8
text: For, Hushai said, you know your father and his men, that they [are] mighty men, and they [are] bitter of soul, like a bear robbed of her cubs in the field. And your father [is] a man of war, and will not stay the night with the people.

title: II Samuel 17:9
text: Behold, he is hidden now in some pit, or in one of the places. And it shall be, at the falling among them at the first, whoever hears will say, There is a slaughter among the people who follow Absalom.

title: II Samuel 17:10
text: And also he, the son of valor, whose heart [is] like the heart of a lion, shall utterly melt. For all Israel knows that your father [is] a mighty man, and they who [are] with him [are] mighty men.

title: II Samuel 17:11
text: Therefore I advise that all Israel be generally gathered to you, from Dan even to Beer-sheba, like the sand that [is] by the sea for multitude. And you yourself shall go into battle.

title: II Samuel 17:12
text: And we shall come upon him in some place where he shall be found, and we will light upon him like the dew falls upon the ground. And of all the men that [are] with him, not even one shall be left.

title: II Samuel 17:13
text: And if he has gotten into a city, then all Israel shall bring ropes to that city, and we will draw it into the river until there is not one small stone found there.

title: II Samuel 17:14
text: And Absalom and all the men of Israel said, The counsel of Hushai the Archite [is] better than the counsel of Ahithophel. For the LORD had appointed to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, to the intent that the LORD might bring evil on Absalom.

title: II Samuel 17:15
text: And Hushai said to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, This and this Ahithophel advised Absalom and the elders of Israel, and this and this I have advised.

title: II Samuel 17:16
text: And now send quickly and tell David, saying, Do not stay in the plains of the wilderness tonight, but speedily pass over, lest the king be swallowed up, and all the people with him.

title: II Samuel 17:17
text: And Jonathan and Ahimaaz stayed by En-rogel, for there they might not be seen to come into the city. And a slave-girl went and told them, and they went and told king David.

title: II Samuel 17:18
text: But a lad saw them and told Absalom. But both of them went away quickly, and came to a man's house in Bahurim, who had a well in his court, into which they went down.

title: II Samuel 17:19
text: And the woman took and spread a covering over the well's mouth, and spread ground grain on it, and the thing was not known.

title: II Samuel 17:20
text: And when Absalom's servants came to the woman, to the house, they said, Where [are] Ahimaaz and Jonathan? And the woman said to them, They have gone over the brook of water. And when they had searched and could not find them, they returned to Jerusalem.

title: II Samuel 17:21
text: And it happened after they had departed, they came up out of the well, and went and told King David. And [they] said to David, Arise and pass quickly over the waters, for this is what Ahithophel has advised against you.

title: II Samuel 17:22
text: Then David and all the people with him arose. And they passed over Jordan. By the morning light there was not one of them that had not gone over Jordan.

title: II Samuel 17:23
text: And when Ahithophel saw that his counsel was not followed, even he saddled the ass and arose, and went home to his house, to his city, and put his household in order. And he hanged himself and died, and was buried in the tomb of his father.

title: II Samuel 17:24
text: And David came to Mahanaim. And Absalom passed over Jordan, he and all the men of Israel with him.

title: II Samuel 17:25
text: And Absalom made Amasa captain of the army instead of Joab. This Amasa [was] the son of a man named Ithra, an Israelite, who went in to Abigail the daughter of Nahash, sister to Zeruiah, Joab's mother.

title: II Samuel 17:26
text: And Israel and Absalom pitched in the land of Gilead.

title: II Samuel 17:27
text: And it happened when David came to Mahanaim, Shobi the son of Nahash of Rabbah, of the sons of Ammon, and Machir the son of Ammiel of Lodebar, and Barzillai the Gileadite of Rogelim,

title: II Samuel 17:28
text: brought beds and basins and earthen vessels, and wheat and barley and flour and roasted [grain], and beans and lentils and other roasted food,

title: II Samuel 17:29
text: and honey and butter and sheep and cheese from cows, for David and for the people with him to eat. For they said, The people [are] hungry and weary and thirsty in the wilderness.

title: II Samuel 18:1
text: And David numbered the people who were with him, and set captains of thousands and captains of hundreds over them.

title: II Samuel 18:2
text: And David sent forth a third of the people under the hand of Joab, and a third under the hand of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother, and a third under the hand of Ittai the Gittite. And the king said to the people, I will also surely go forth with you myself.

title: II Samuel 18:3
text: But the people answered, You shall not go forth. For if we run away, they will not set [their] heart on us, even if half of us die. For now you [are] worth ten thousand of us. And now [it is] better that you remain to help us from the city.

title: II Samuel 18:4
text: And the king said to them, I will do what is good in your eyes. And the king stood by the side of the gate, and all the people came out by hundreds and by thousands.

title: II Samuel 18:5
text: And the king commanded Joab and Abishai and Ittai, saying, For my sake be gentle with the young man, with Absalom. And all the people heard when the king gave all the commanders charge concerning Absalom.

title: II Samuel 18:6
text: And the people went out into the field against Israel. And the battle was in the forest of Ephraim.

title: II Samuel 18:7
text: And the people of Israel were killed there before the servants of David. And there was a great slaughter that day of twenty thousand.

title: II Samuel 18:8
text: For the battle was scattered there over the face of all the country. And the forest devoured more people that day than the sword devoured.

title: II Samuel 18:9
text: And Absalom met the servants of David. And Absalom rode on a mule, and the mule went under the thick boughs of a great oak. And his head caught hold of the oak, and he was taken up between the heavens and the earth. And the mule under him went away.

title: II Samuel 18:10
text: And a certain man saw and told Joab, and said, Behold, I saw Absalom hanged in an oak.

title: II Samuel 18:11
text: And Joab said to the man who told him, And, behold, you saw [him], and why did you not strike him there to the ground? And I would have given you ten shekels of silver and a girdle.

title: II Samuel 18:12
text: And the man said to Joab, Though I should receive a thousand silverlings in my hand, yet I would not put forth my hand against the king's son. For in our ears the king charged you and Abishai and Ittai, saying, Beware you who go against the young man, against Absalom.

title: II Samuel 18:13
text: Or I would have dealt falsely with my own life, for there is no matter hidden from the king, and you yourself would have set yourself against [me].

title: II Samuel 18:14
text: And Joab said, I cannot stay here with you this way! And he took three darts in his hand and thrust them through the heart of Absalom while he [was] still alive in the midst of the oak.

title: II Samuel 18:15
text: And ten young men who bore Joab's armor surrounded and struck Absalom, and killed him.

title: II Samuel 18:16
text: And Joab blew the ram's horn, and the people returned from pursuing Israel. For Joab held back the people.

title: II Samuel 18:17
text: And they took Absalom and threw him into a great pit in the forest. And they laid a very great heap of stones upon him. And all Israel fled, each one to his tent.

title: II Samuel 18:18
text: And Absalom in his lifetime had taken and reared up for himself a pillar, which [is] in the King's Valley. For he said, I have no son to keep my name in remembrance. And he called the pillar after his own name. And it is called until this day, Absalom's monument.

title: II Samuel 18:19
text: Then Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said, And let me run and bear the news to the king, how the LORD has avenged him of his enemies.

title: II Samuel 18:20
text: And Joab said to him, You shall not bear news today, but you shall bear good news some other day. But today you shall bear no tidings, because the king's son is dead.

title: II Samuel 18:21
text: And Joab said to Cushi, Go tell the king what you have seen. And Cushi bowed himself to Joab, and ran.

title: II Samuel 18:22
text: And Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said yet again to Joab, Yet whatever, please let me also run after the Cushite. And Joab said, Why will you run, my son, since you have no good news ready?

title: II Samuel 18:23
text: But he said, Yet whatever, let me run! And he said to him, Run. And Ahimaaz ran by the way of the plain, and ran past the Cushite.

title: II Samuel 18:24
text: And David sat between the two gates. And the watchman went up to the roof over the gate to the wall, and lifted up his eyes and looked. And behold, a man ran alone.

title: II Samuel 18:25
text: And the watchman cried and told the king. And the king said, If he [is] alone, there is news in his mouth. And he came apace and drew near.

title: II Samuel 18:26
text: And the watchman saw another man running. And the watchman called to the porter and said, Behold, [another] man running alone. And the king said, He also brings news.

title: II Samuel 18:27
text: And the watchman said, I see the running of the first is like the running of Ahimaaz the son of Zadok. And the king said, He [is] a good man, and comes with good news.

title: II Samuel 18:28
text: And Ahimaaz called and said to the king, Peace! And he fell down upon his face before the king, and said, Blessed [be] the LORD your God, who has delivered up the men who lifted up their hand against my lord the king.

title: II Samuel 18:29
text: And the king said, Peace to the young man, to Absalom? And Ahimaaz answered, When Joab sent the king's servant, and your servant, I saw a great uproar, but I did not know what [it was].

title: II Samuel 18:30
text: And the king said, Turn aside, stand here. And he turned aside and stood still.

title: II Samuel 18:31
text: And, behold, Cushi came. And Cushi said, Good news, my lord the king, for the LORD has avenged you this day of all those who rose up against you.

title: II Samuel 18:32
text: And the king said to Cushi, Peace to the young man, to Absalom? And Cushi answered, May the enemies of my lord the king, and all who rise against you to do [you] hurt, be as the young man.

title: II Samuel 18:33
text: And the king was much moved, and went up to the room over the gate and wept. And as he went, he said this, O my son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! Would God I had died for you, O Absalom, my son, my son!

title: II Samuel 19:1
text: And it was told to Joab, Behold, the king weeps and mourns for Absalom.

title: II Samuel 19:2
text: And the victory that day was [turned] into mourning to all the people. For the people heard it said that day how the king was grieved for his son.

title: II Samuel 19:3
text: And the people went up secretly into the city that day, as people who are ashamed steal away when they flee in battle.

title: II Samuel 19:4
text: But the king covered his face, and the king cried [with] a loud voice, O my son Absalom, O Absalom, my son, my son!

title: II Samuel 19:5
text: And Joab came into the house to the king and said, You have today shamed the faces of all your servants. For they have saved your life and the lives of your sons and your daughters today, the lives of your wives, and the lives of your concubines.

title: II Samuel 19:6
text: By loving your enemies and hating those who love you, you have declared today that there are neither commanders nor servants to you. For I know that today if Absalom had lived and all of us had died today, then it would have pleased you very much!

title: II Samuel 19:7
text: And now get up and go out. Speak to the heart of your servants. For I swear by the LORD [if] you do not go out, not a man shall stay with you tonight. And that will be worse to you than all the evil which has come to you from your youth until now.

title: II Samuel 19:8
text: Then the king arose and sat in the gate. And they told it to the people, saying, Behold, the king sits in the gate! And all the people came before the king. (For Israel had fled, every one to his tent.)

title: II Samuel 19:9
text: And it happened, all the people quarreled throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, The king saved us out of the hand of our enemies, and he delivered us out of the hand of the Philistines. And now he has fled out of the land from Absalom.

title: II Samuel 19:10
text: And Absalom, whom we anointed over us, [is] dead in battle. And now why do you not speak a word about bringing the king back?

title: II Samuel 19:11
text: And king David sent to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, saying, Speak to the elders of Judah, saying, Why are you the last to bring the king back to his house? For the word of all Israel has come to the king, to his house.

title: II Samuel 19:12
text: You [are] my brothers, and my flesh and my bone. Why then are you the last to bring back the king?

title: II Samuel 19:13
text: And you say to Amasa, [Are] you not of my bone and of my flesh? May God do so to me, and more also, if you are not commander of the army before me all the days instead of Joab.

title: II Samuel 19:14
text: And he bowed [the heart of] all the men of Judah, even as one man, so that they sent to the king, saying, Return, you and all your servants.

title: II Samuel 19:15
text: And the king returned and came to Jordan. And Judah came to Gilgal to go to meet the king, to conduct the king over Jordan.

title: II Samuel 19:16
text: And Shimei the son of Gera, the Benjamite from Bahurim, hurried and came down with the men of Judah to meet king David.

title: II Samuel 19:17
text: And a thousand men of Benjamin were with him, and Ziba the servant of the house of Saul, and his fifteen sons and his twenty servants with him. And they went over Jordan before the king.

title: II Samuel 19:18
text: And they had crossed over the ford to carry over the king's household, and to do what he thought good. And Shimei the son of Gera fell down before the king as he had come over Jordan.

title: II Samuel 19:19
text: And [he] said to the king, Let not my lord charge iniquity to me. Do not remember the perverse way your servant acted in the day that my lord the king went out of Jerusalem, for the king to take it to his heart.

title: II Samuel 19:20
text: For your servant knows that I have sinned. And, behold, I come today, the first of all the house of Joseph to go down to meet my lord the king.

title: II Samuel 19:21
text: But Abishai the son of Zeruiah answered and said, Shall not Shimei be put to death for this, because he cursed the LORD's anointed?

title: II Samuel 19:22
text: And David said, What do I have to do with you, you sons of Zeruiah, that you should be my foes today? Shall there be [any] man put to death today in Israel? For do I not know that I [am] king over Israel today?

title: II Samuel 19:23
text: And the king said to Shimei, You shall not die. And the king swore to him.

title: II Samuel 19:24
text: And Mephibosheth the son of Saul came down to meet the king. And he had neither dressed his feet, nor trimmed his moustache, nor washed his clothes, from the day the king departed until he came in peace.

title: II Samuel 19:25
text: And it happened when he had come to Jerusalem to meet the king, the king said to him, Why did you not go with me, Mephibosheth?

title: II Samuel 19:26
text: And he answered, My lord, O, king, my servant deceived me. For your servant said, I will saddle me an ass so that I may ride on it and go to the king, because your servant [is] lame.

title: II Samuel 19:27
text: And he spoke slander against your servant to my lord the king. But my lord the king [is] as an angel of God. And do [what is] good in your eyes.

title: II Samuel 19:28
text: For all my father's house were but dead men before my lord the king. And you set your servant among those eating at your own table. What right then have I to cry to the king any more?

title: II Samuel 19:29
text: And the king said to him, Why do you speak any more of your matters? I have said, You and Ziba divide the land.

title: II Samuel 19:30
text: And Mephibosheth said to the king, Yes, let him take all, because my lord the king has come in peace to his own house.

title: II Samuel 19:31
text: And Barzillai of Gilead came down from Rogelim, and went over Jordan with the king to conduct him over Jordan.

title: II Samuel 19:32
text: And Barzillai was a very aged man, eighty years old. And he had provided food for the king while he abode at Mahanaim, for he [was] a very great man.

title: II Samuel 19:33
text: And the king said to Barzillai, Come over with me and I will sustain you with me in Jerusalem.

title: II Samuel 19:34
text: And Barzillai said to the king, How long do I have to live, that I should go up with the king to Jerusalem?

title: II Samuel 19:35
text: I [am] eighty years old today, [and] can I discern between good and evil? Can your servant taste what I eat or what I drink? Can I any more hear the voice of singing men and singing women? Why then should your servant be still a burden to my lord the king?

title: II Samuel 19:36
text: Your servant will go a little [way] over Jordan with the king. And why should the king repay me with such a reward?

title: II Samuel 19:37
text: Please let your servant return so that I may die in my own city by the grave of my father and of my mother. But behold your servant Chimham, let him go over with my lord the king. And do to him what shall seem good to you.

title: II Samuel 19:38
text: And the king answered, Chimham shall go over with me, and I will do to him that which shall seem good to you. And whatever you shall ask of me, that I will do for you.

title: II Samuel 19:39
text: And all the people went over Jordan. And when the king had come over, the king kissed Barzillai, and blessed him. And he returned to his place.

title: II Samuel 19:40
text: And the king went on to Gilgal, and Chimham went on with him. And all the people of Judah were bringing the king, and also half the people of Israel.

title: II Samuel 19:41
text: And, behold, all the men of Israel came to the king, and said to the king, Why have our brothers the men of Judah stolen you away, and have brought the king and his household, and all David's men with him, over Jordan?

title: II Samuel 19:42
text: And all the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, Because the king [is] near to us. Why then are you angry for this matter? Have we eaten at all at the king's [cost]? Or has he given us any gift?

title: II Samuel 19:43
text: And the men of Israel answered the men of Judah and said, We have ten parts in the king, and we also have more [right] in David than you. Why then did you despise us, so that our advice should not be sought first in bringing back our king? And the words of the men of Judah were more fierce than the words of the men of Israel.

title: II Samuel 20:1
text: And there happened to be there a man of Belial named Sheba, the son of Bichri, a Benjamite. And he blew a ram's horn and said, We have no part in David, neither do we have any inheritance in the son of Jesse. Every man to his tents, O, Israel!

title: II Samuel 20:2
text: And every man of Israel went up from after David, following Sheba the son of Bichri. But the men of Judah clung to their king, from Jordan even to Jerusalem.

title: II Samuel 20:3
text: And David came to his house at Jerusalem. And the king took the ten women, [his] concubines, whom he had left to keep the house, and put them in ward, and fed them but did not go in to them. And they were shut up till the day of their death, living in widowhood.

title: II Samuel 20:4
text: And the king said to Amasa, gather to me the men of Judah [within] three days, and you be present here.

title: II Samuel 20:5
text: And Amasa went to gather Judah. But he stayed longer than the set time which he had appointed him.

title: II Samuel 20:6
text: And David said to Abishai, And Sheba the son of Bichri shall do us more harm than Absalom. You take your lord's servants and pursue him, lest he get himself into fortified cities and escape us.

title: II Samuel 20:7
text: And Joab's men went out after him, and the Cherethites, and the Pelethites, and all the mighty men. And they went out of Jerusalem to pursue Sheba the son of Bichri.

title: II Samuel 20:8
text: They [were] at the great stone which [is] in Gibeon, and Amasa had gone before them. And Joab was girded [with] his war-coat as his clothing. And upon it was a girdle with a sword fastened upon his loins, in its sheath. And as he went forth, it fell out.

title: II Samuel 20:9
text: And Joab said to Amasa, [Are] you well, my brother? And Joab took Amasa by the beard with the right hand to kiss him.

title: II Samuel 20:10
text: And Amasa was not on guard against the sword that [was] in Joab's hand. And he struck him with it in the belly, and poured out his bowels to the ground. And [he] did not strike him again. And he died. And Joab and Abishai his brother pursued after Sheba the son of Bichri.

title: II Samuel 20:11
text: And one of Joab's men stood by him and said, He who favors Joab, and he who [is] for David, [go] after Joab!

title: II Samuel 20:12
text: And Amasa wallowed in blood in the middle of the highway. And the man saw that all the people stood still. And he moved Amasa out of the highway into the field, and threw a garment over him when he saw that everyone who came by him stood still.

title: II Samuel 20:13
text: When he was moved out of the highway, all the people went on after Joab, to pursue after Sheba the son of Bichri.

title: II Samuel 20:14
text: And he went through all the tribes of Israel to Abel, and to Beth-maachah, and to all the Berites. And they were gathered, and went after him too.

title: II Samuel 20:15
text: And they came and besieged him in Abel of Beth-maachah. And they threw up a siege-mound against the city. And it stood against the wall. And all the people with Joab were undermining the wall to make it fall.

title: II Samuel 20:16
text: Then a wise woman cried out of the city, Hear, hear! Please say to Joab, Come near here so that I may speak with you.

title: II Samuel 20:17
text: And when he had come near her, the woman said, [Are] you Joab? And he answered, I [am]. And she said to him, Hear the words of your handmaid. And he answered, I hear.

title: II Samuel 20:18
text: And she spoke, saying, They spoke often in days gone by, saying, Surely they will ask of Abel, and so they ended [the matter].

title: II Samuel 20:19
text: I [am] peaceable [and] faithful in Israel. You seek to destroy a city and a mother in Israel. Why will you swallow up the inheritance of the LORD?

title: II Samuel 20:20
text: And Joab answered and said, Far be it, far be it from me, that I should swallow up or destroy.

title: II Samuel 20:21
text: The matter [is] not so. But a man of mount Ephraim, Sheba the son of Bichri by name, has lifted up his hand against the king, against David. Only deliver him, and I will depart from the city. And the woman said to Joab, Behold, his head shall be thrown to you over the wall.

title: II Samuel 20:22
text: Then the woman went to all the people in her wisdom. And they cut off the head of Sheba the son of Bichri, and threw [it] out to Joab. And he blew the ram's horn, and they scattered from the city, each man to his tent. And Joab returned to Jerusalem to the king.

title: II Samuel 20:23
text: And Joab [was] over all the army of Israel. And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada [was] over the Cherethites and over the Pelethites.

title: II Samuel 20:24
text: And Adoram [was] over the tribute. And Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud [was] recorder.

title: II Samuel 20:25
text: And Sheva [was] scribe. And Zadok and Abiathar [were] the priests.

title: II Samuel 20:26
text: And also Ira the Jairite was a chief ruler around David.

title: II Samuel 21:1
text: And there was a famine in the days of David three years, year after year. And David inquired of the LORD. And the LORD answered, For Saul, and for [his] bloody house, because he killed the Gibeonites.

title: II Samuel 21:2
text: And the king called the Gibeonites and spoke to them. And the Gibeonites [were] not of the sons of Israel, but of the remnant of the Amorites. And the sons of Israel had sworn to them. And Saul sought to kill them in his zeal to the sons of Israel and Judah.

title: II Samuel 21:3
text: And David said to the Gibeonites, What shall I do for you? And with what shall I atone for this, so that you may bless the inheritance of the LORD?

title: II Samuel 21:4
text: And the Gibeonites said to him, We will have no silver nor gold from Saul, nor from his house. Also, we will have no man in Israel put to death. And he said, What you shall say, I will do for you.

title: II Samuel 21:5
text: And they answered the king, The man who destroyed us, and who devised against us, that we should be destroyed from remaining in any of the borders of Israel

title: II Samuel 21:6
text: let seven men of his sons be delivered to us, and we will hang them up to the Lord in Gibeah of Saul, the chosen of the LORD. And the king said, I will give [them].

title: II Samuel 21:7
text: But the king spared Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan the son of Saul, because of the LORD's oath that [was] between them, between David and Jonathan the son of Saul.

title: II Samuel 21:8
text: But the king took the two sons of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, whom she bore to Saul, Armoni and Mephibosheth, and the five sons of Michal the daughter of Saul, whom she bore to Adriel the son of Barzillai the Meholathite.

title: II Samuel 21:9
text: And he delivered them into the hands of the Gibeonites. And they hanged them in the hill before the LORD. And they fell, seven together, and were put to death in the days of harvest, in the first [days], in the beginning of barley harvest.

title: II Samuel 21:10
text: And Rizpah the daughter of Aiah took sackcloth and spread it for herself upon the rock, from the beginning of harvest until water dropped upon them out of heaven. And she did not allow either the birds of the air to rest on them by day, nor the beasts of the field by night.

title: II Samuel 21:11
text: And it was told David what Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, the concubine of Saul, had done.

title: II Samuel 21:12
text: And David went and took the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son from the men of Jabesh-gilead, who had stolen them from the street of Beth-shan, where the Philistines had hanged them when the Philistines had slain Saul in Gilboa.

title: II Samuel 21:13
text: And he brought the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son up from there. And they gathered the bones of those who were hanged.

title: II Samuel 21:14
text: And [they] buried the bones of Saul and Jonathan his son in the land of Benjamin in Zelah, in the tomb of his father Kish. And they did all that the king commanded. And afterward God heeded prayer for the land.

title: II Samuel 21:15
text: And again the Philistines warred with Israel. And David went down, and his servants with him, and fought against the Philistines. And David became faint.

title: II Samuel 21:16
text: And Ishbi-benob, who [was] of the sons of the giant, the weight of whose spear [was] three hundred shekels of bronze in weight. And he being girded with a new [sword] thought to kill David.

title: II Samuel 21:17
text: But Abishai the son of Zeruiah came to his aid, and struck the Philistine, and killed him. Then the men of David swore to him, saying, You shall not go out to battle with us any more, so that you do not put out the light of Israel.

title: II Samuel 21:18
text: And it happened after this there was again a battle with the Philistines at Gob. Then Sibbechai the Hushathite killed Saph, who [was] of the sons of the giant.

title: II Samuel 21:19
text: And there was again a battle with the Philistines in Gob, where Elhanan of Bethlehem, the son of Jaare-oregim, killed one of Goliath the Gittite, the staff of whose spear [was] like a weaver's beam.

title: II Samuel 21:20
text: And there was yet again a battle in Gath. And there was a man of stature who had six fingers on each hand, and six toes on each foot, twenty-four in number. And he also was born to the giant.

title: II Samuel 21:21
text: And when he defied Israel, Jonathan the son of Shimeah, the brother of David, killed him.

title: II Samuel 21:22
text: These four were born to the giant in Gath, and fell by the hand of David, and by the hand of his servants.

title: II Samuel 22:1
text: And David spoke to the LORD the words of this song in the day the LORD had delivered him out of the hand of all his enemies, and out of the hand of Saul.

title: II Samuel 22:2
text: And he said, The LORD [is] my Rock, and my Fortress, and my Deliverer.

title: II Samuel 22:3
text: The God who is my Rock, in Him will I trust. [He is] my Shield, and the Horn of my salvation, my High Tower, and my Refuge, my Savior. You save me from violence.

title: II Samuel 22:4
text: I will call upon the LORD, [who is] worthy to be praised. And I shall be saved from my enemies.

title: II Samuel 22:5
text: When the waves of death encircled me, the floods of ungodly men made me afraid.

title: II Samuel 22:6
text: The sorrows of hell hemmed me in. The snares of death went in front of me.

title: II Samuel 22:7
text: In my distress I called upon the LORD and cried to my God. And he heard my voice out of His temple, and my cry [entered] into His ears.

title: II Samuel 22:8
text: And the earth shook and trembled. The foundations of the heavens moved and shook because He was angry.

title: II Samuel 22:9
text: Smoke went up out of His nostrils, and fire out of His mouth devoured. Coals were kindled by it.

title: II Samuel 22:10
text: He bowed the heavens also, and came down. And darkness [was] under His feet.

title: II Samuel 22:11
text: And He rode upon a cherub and did fly. And [He] was seen upon the wings of the wind.

title: II Samuel 22:12
text: And He made darkness coverings around Him, dark waters, thick clouds of the skies.

title: II Samuel 22:13
text: From the brightness before Him were coals of fire kindled.

title: II Samuel 22:14
text: The LORD thundered from the heavens, and the Most High uttered His voice.

title: II Samuel 22:15
text: And He sent out arrows, and scattered them; lightning, and troubled them.

title: II Samuel 22:16
text: And the channels of the sea appeared, the foundations of the world were uncovered, at the rebuking of the LORD, at the blast of the breath of His nostrils.

title: II Samuel 22:17
text: He sent from above, He took me. He drew me out of many waters.

title: II Samuel 22:18
text: He delivered me from my strong enemy, from those who hated me; for they were stronger than I.

title: II Samuel 22:19
text: They went before me in the day of my calamity, but the LORD was my stay.

title: II Samuel 22:20
text: He brought me forth also into a large place. He delivered me because He delighted in me.

title: II Samuel 22:21
text: The LORD rewarded me according to my righteousness, according to the cleanness of my hands He has rewarded me.

title: II Samuel 22:22
text: For I have kept the ways of the LORD, and have not wickedly departed from my God.

title: II Samuel 22:23
text: For all His judgments [were] before me. And as for His statutes, I did not depart from them.

title: II Samuel 22:24
text: I was also upright before Him, and have kept myself from my iniquity.

title: II Samuel 22:25
text: And the LORD rewarded me according to my righteousness, according to my cleanness in His eyes.

title: II Samuel 22:26
text: With the faithful You will show Yourself faithful; with the upright man You will show Yourself upright.

title: II Samuel 22:27
text: With the pure You will show Yourself pure; and with the perverted You will appear perverse.

title: II Samuel 22:28
text: And You will save the afflicted people, but Your eyes [are] on the proud, [whom] You bring low.

title: II Samuel 22:29
text: For You [are] my lamp, O LORD. And the LORD will lighten my darkness.

title: II Samuel 22:30
text: For by You I have run [through] a troop. By my God I have leaped over a wall.

title: II Samuel 22:31
text: [As for] God, His way [is] perfect. The word of the LORD [is] tried. He is a shield to all those who seek refuge in Him.

title: II Samuel 22:32
text: For who [is] God, except Jehovah? And who [is] a rock except our God?

title: II Samuel 22:33
text: God [is] my strength [and] power, and He makes my way perfect.

title: II Samuel 22:34
text: [He] makes my feet like hinds' [feet], and causing me to stand on my high places.

title: II Samuel 22:35
text: He teaches my hands to war, so that my hands may bend a bow of bronze.

title: II Samuel 22:36
text: You have also given me the shield of Your salvation, and Your gentleness has made me great.

title: II Samuel 22:37
text: You have enlarged my steps under me, so that my feet did not slip.

title: II Samuel 22:38
text: I have pursued my enemies and destroyed them, and turned not again until I had finished them.

title: II Samuel 22:39
text: And I have crushed them and wounded them so that they could not rise. [Yea], they have fallen under my feet.

title: II Samuel 22:40
text: For You have girded me [with] strength to battle. You have subdued under me those who rose up against me.

title: II Samuel 22:41
text: You have also given me the necks of my enemies; I silenced those who hate me.

title: II Samuel 22:42
text: They looked, but [there was] none to save; to the LORD, but He did not answer them.

title: II Samuel 22:43
text: Then I beat them as small as the dust of the earth, I stamped them like the mire of the streets [and] spread them out.

title: II Samuel 22:44
text: You have also delivered me from the strivings of my people, You have kept me the head of the nations. A people I knew not shall serve me.

title: II Samuel 22:45
text: Strangers shall submit themselves to me. As soon as they hear, they shall obey me.

title: II Samuel 22:46
text: Strangers shall fade away, and they shall be afraid out of their strongholds.

title: II Samuel 22:47
text: The LORD lives! And blessed [be] my Rock, and exalted be the God, the Rock of my salvation.

title: II Samuel 22:48
text: It [is] God who avenges me and who brings down the peoples under me,

title: II Samuel 22:49
text: and who brings me forth from my enemies. You also lift me up on high above those rising up against me. You deliver me from the violent man.

title: II Samuel 22:50
text: Therefore, I will give thanks to You, O LORD, among the heathen, and I will sing praises to Your name.

title: II Samuel 22:51
text: [He is] the Tower of salvation for His king, and He shows mercy to His anointed, to David and to his seed, forevermore.

title: II Samuel 23:1
text: And these [are] the last words of David. David the son of Jesse said, and the man who was raised up on high, the anointed of the God of Jacob, and the sweet psalmist of Israel, said:

title: II Samuel 23:2
text: The Spirit of the LORD spoke by me, and His word [was] in my tongue.

title: II Samuel 23:3
text: The God of Israel said, The Rock of Israel spoke to me: he who rules over men justly, ruling [in] the fear of God,

title: II Samuel 23:4
text: is as the light of the morning, as the sun rises, a morning without clouds. The tender grass [springs] out of the earth through shining after rain.

title: II Samuel 23:5
text: Although my house [is] not so with God, yet He has made with me an everlasting covenant, ordered in all things, and sure. For all my salvation, and all my desire, will He not make it grow?

title: II Samuel 23:6
text: But the wicked, all of them, [shall be] like a thorn thrust away, because they cannot be taken by the hand.

title: II Samuel 23:7
text: But the man who shall touch them must be armed with iron and the staff of a spear. And they shall be utterly burned in [their] place.

title: II Samuel 23:8
text: These [are] the names of the mighty men whom David had: Josheb-basshebeth the Tachmonite, chief of the three; he [was called] Adino the Eznite, because of the eight hundred [he] killed at one time.

title: II Samuel 23:9
text: And after him [was] Eleazar the son of Dodo the Ahohite, one of the three mighty men with David when they defied the Philistines who were gathered there to battle; and the men of Israel had gone up;

title: II Samuel 23:10
text: [he] arose and struck the Philistines until his hand was weary, and until his hand clung to the sword. And the LORD worked a great victory that day. And the people returned after him only to spoil.

title: II Samuel 23:11
text: And next [was] Shammah the son of Agee the Hararite. And the Philistines were gathered together into a troop, where there was a piece of ground full of lentils. And the people fled from the Philistines.

title: II Samuel 23:12
text: But he stood in the middle of the ground and delivered it, and killed the Philistines. And the LORD worked a great victory.

title: II Samuel 23:13
text: And three of the thirty chief men went down and came to David in the harvest time into the cave of Adullam. And the troop of the Philistines pitched in the Valley of the Giants.

title: II Samuel 23:14
text: And David [was] then in a stronghold, and the fort of the Philistines [was] then in Bethlehem.

title: II Samuel 23:15
text: And David longed and said, Oh that someone would give me a drink from the water of the well of Bethlehem by the gate!

title: II Samuel 23:16
text: And the three mighty men broke through the army of the Philistines, and drew water out of the well of Bethlehem by the gate, and took [it], and brought [it] to David. But he would not drink of it, but poured it out to the LORD.

title: II Samuel 23:17
text: And he said, Be it far from me, O LORD, that I should do this. [Is it not] the blood of the men who went [in danger of] their lives? And he would not drink it. These three mighty men did these [things].

title: II Samuel 23:18
text: And Abishai the brother of Joab, the son of Zeruiah, [was] chief among three. And he lifted up his spear against three hundred [and] killed [them], and had the name among three.

title: II Samuel 23:19
text: Surely he was honored more than the three. And he was their commander. However he did not attain to the [first] three.

title: II Samuel 23:20
text: And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada from Kabzeel, a son of a mighty man, great [in] deeds. He killed two lion-like men of Moab. He went down also and killed a lion in the middle of a pit in time of snow.

title: II Samuel 23:21
text: And he killed an Egyptian, a man of form. And the Egyptian had a spear in his hand, but he went down to him with a staff and plucked the spear out of the Egyptian's hand, and killed him with his own spear.

title: II Samuel 23:22
text: These [things] did Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and had the name among three mighty ones.

title: II Samuel 23:23
text: He was more honorable than the thirty, but he did not attain to the [first] three. And David set him over his guard.

title: II Samuel 23:24
text: Asahel the brother of Joab [was] of the thirty; Elhanan the son of Dodo of Bethlehem;

title: II Samuel 23:25
text: Shammah the Harodite; Elika the Harodite;

title: II Samuel 23:26
text: Helez the Paltite; Ira the son of Ikkesh, the Tekoite;

title: II Samuel 23:27
text: Abiezer the Anathothite; Mebunnai the Hushathite;

title: II Samuel 23:28
text: Zalmon the Ahohite; Maharai the Netophathite;

title: II Samuel 23:29
text: Heleb the son of Baanah, a Netophathite; Ittai the son of Ribai out of Gibeah, of the sons of Benjamin;

title: II Samuel 23:30
text: Benaiah the Pirathonite; Hiddai of the brooks of Gaash;

title: II Samuel 23:31
text: Abialbon the Arbathite; Azmaveth the Barhumite;

title: II Samuel 23:32
text: Eliahba the Shaalbonite, of the sons of Jashen; Jonathan;

title: II Samuel 23:33
text: Shammah the Hararite; Ahiam the son of Sharer, the Hararite;

title: II Samuel 23:34
text: Eliphelet the son of Ahasbai, the son of the Maachathite; Eliam the son of Ahithophel, the Gilonite;

title: II Samuel 23:35
text: Hezrai the Carmelite; Paarai the Arbite;

title: II Samuel 23:36
text: Igal the son of Nathan of Zobah; Bani the Gadite;

title: II Samuel 23:37
text: Zelek the Ammonite; Naharai the Beerothite, armor-bearer to Joab the son of Zeruiah;

title: II Samuel 23:38
text: Ira, and Ithrite; Gareb, and Ithrite;

title: II Samuel 23:39
text: Uriah the Hittite-- thirty-seven in all.

title: II Samuel 24:1
text: And again the anger of the LORD was kindled against Israel, and He moved David against them to say, Go count Israel and Judah.

title: II Samuel 24:2
text: For the king said to Joab the commander of the army, who [was] with him, Go around through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan to Beer-sheba, and count the people so that I may know the number of the people.

title: II Samuel 24:3
text: And Joab said to the king, And may the LORD your God add to the people however many they be, a hundred times as many, and may the eyes of my lord the king may see. But why does my lord the king delight in this thing?

title: II Samuel 24:4
text: But the king's word prevailed against Joab, and against the commanders of the army. And Joab and the commanders of the army went out from the presence of the king to number the people of Israel.

title: II Samuel 24:5
text: And they passed over Jordan and pitched in Aroer, on the right side of the city that [is] in the middle of the Valley of Gad, and to Jazer.

title: II Samuel 24:6
text: And they came to Gilead, and to the land of Tahtim-hodshi. And they came to Dan-jaan, and around to Sidon.

title: II Samuel 24:7
text: And they came to the stronghold of Tyre, and to all the cities of the Hivites and [of] the Canaanites; and went out to the south of Judah, to Beer-sheba.

title: II Samuel 24:8
text: And they went to and fro through all the land, and came to Jerusalem at the end of nine months and twenty days.

title: II Samuel 24:9
text: And Joab gave the sum of the number of the people to the king. And there were in Israel eight hundred thousand strong men who drew the sword. And the men of Judah [were] five hundred thousand men.

title: II Samuel 24:10
text: And David's heart struck him after he had numbered the people. And David said to the LORD, I have sinned greatly in what I have done. And now, I beseech You, O LORD, take away the iniquity of Your servant, for I have done very foolishly.

title: II Samuel 24:11
text: And David rose up in the morning. And the word of the LORD came to the prophet Gad, David's seer, saying,

title: II Samuel 24:12
text: Go and say to David, So says the LORD, I offer you three [things]. Choose one of them, so that I may do [it] to you.

title: II Samuel 24:13
text: And Gad came to David, and told him, and said to him, Shall seven years of famine come upon you and on your land? Or will you flee three months before your enemies while they pursue you? Or shall there be three days' plague in your land? And advise, and see what answer I shall return to Him who sent me.

title: II Samuel 24:14
text: And David said to Gad, I [am] in great distress. Let us fall now into the hand of the LORD, for His mercies [are] great. And do not let me fall into the hand of man.

title: II Samuel 24:15
text: And the LORD sent a plague upon Israel from the morning even till the time appointed. And there died from the people, from Dan to Beer-sheba, seventy thousand men.

title: II Samuel 24:16
text: And when the angel stretched out his hand upon Jerusalem to destroy it, the LORD turned from the evil, and said to the angel who destroyed the people, Enough! And stay your hand. And the angel of the LORD was by the threshing-place of Araunah the Jebusite.

title: II Samuel 24:17
text: And David spoke to the LORD when he saw the angel who struck the people, and said, Lo, I have sinned, and I have done wickedly. But these sheep, what have they done? I pray You, let Your hand be against me and against my father's house.

title: II Samuel 24:18
text: And Gad came that day to David, and said to him, Go up! Rear an altar to the LORD in the threshing-floor of Araunah the Jebusite.

title: II Samuel 24:19
text: And David went up, according to the saying of Gad, as the LORD commanded.

title: II Samuel 24:20
text: And Araunah looked and saw the king and his servants coming on toward him. And Araunah went out and bowed before the king, his face to the ground.

title: II Samuel 24:21
text: And Araunah said, Why has my lord the king come to his servant? And David said, To buy the threshing-floor from you, to build an altar to the LORD, so that the plague may be stayed from the people.

title: II Samuel 24:22
text: And Araunah said to David, Let my lord the king take and offer up what [seems] good to him. Behold, oxen for burnt sacrifice, and threshing instruments, and instruments of the oxen for wood.

title: II Samuel 24:23
text: All these Araunah, like a king, gave to the king. And Araunah said to the king, May the LORD your God accept you.

title: II Samuel 24:24
text: And the king said to Araunah, No, but I will surely buy from you at a price. And I will not offer burnt offerings to the LORD my God [of that which costs me] nothing. And David bought the threshing-floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.

title: II Samuel 24:25
text: And David built there an altar to the LORD, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. And the LORD was entreated for the land, and the plague was stayed from Israel.

title: I Kings 1:1
text: And king David was old, going on in days. And they covered him with clothes, but he got no heat.

title: I Kings 1:2
text: And his servants said to him, Let there be sought for my lord the king a young virgin. And let her stand before the king, and let her nurse him, and let her lie in your bosom, so that my lord the king may get heat.

title: I Kings 1:3
text: And they sought out a beautiful girl throughout all the borders of Israel, and found Abishag, a Shunammite. And they brought her to the king.

title: I Kings 1:4
text: And the girl [was] very beautiful. And she nursed the king and served him. But the king did not know her.

title: I Kings 1:5
text: And Adonijah the son of Haggith exalted himself, saying, I will be king. And he prepared himself chariots and horsemen, and fifty men to run before him.

title: I Kings 1:6
text: And his father had not displeased him at any time, saying, Why have you done so? And he also [was] very good of form, and [his mother] bore him after Absalom.

title: I Kings 1:7
text: And he talked with Joab the son of Zeruiah, and with Abiathar the priest. And they helped Adonijah, following [him].

title: I Kings 1:8
text: But Zadok the priest, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and Nathan the prophet, and Shimei, and Rei, and David's mighty men, were not with Adonijah.

title: I Kings 1:9
text: And Adonijah killed sheep and oxen and fat cattle by the Stone of Serpents, which [is] by En-rogel, and called all his brothers, the king's sons, and all the men of Judah, the king's servants.

title: I Kings 1:10
text: But he did not call Nathan the prophet and Benaiah and the mighty men, and Solomon his brother.

title: I Kings 1:11
text: And Nathan spoke to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon, saying, Have you not heard that Adonijah the son of Haggith reigns, and David our lord does not know?

title: I Kings 1:12
text: And now come, please let me give you counsel, and save your own life and the life of your son Solomon.

title: I Kings 1:13
text: Go up and go in to king David, and say to him, My lord, O king, did you not swear to your handmaid, saying, Surely your son Solomon shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne? Why then does Adonijah reign?

title: I Kings 1:14
text: Behold, while you are still talking with the king, I also will come in after you and confirm your words.

title: I Kings 1:15
text: And Bathsheba went in to the king into the room. And the king [was] very old, and Abishag the Shunammite served the king.

title: I Kings 1:16
text: And Bathsheba bowed and knelt before the king. And the king said, What [shall I do] for you?

title: I Kings 1:17
text: And she said to him, My lord, you swore by the LORD your God to your handmaid, [saying], Surely your son Solomon shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne.

title: I Kings 1:18
text: And now, behold, Adonijah reigns. And now, my lord, you do not know.

title: I Kings 1:19
text: And he has slain oxen and fat cattle and sheep in abundance, and has called all the sons of the king, and Abiathar the priest, and Joab the commander of the army. But he has not called your servant Solomon.

title: I Kings 1:20
text: And you, my lord, O king, the eyes of all Israel [are] upon you, that you should tell them who shall sit upon the throne of my lord the king after him.

title: I Kings 1:21
text: And it will be, when my lord the king shall sleep with his fathers, my son Solomon and I shall be offenders.

title: I Kings 1:22
text: And lo, she was still talking with the king, and Nathan the prophet came in.

title: I Kings 1:23
text: And they told the king, saying, Behold, Nathan the prophet. And he came in before the king, and bowed before the king with his face to the ground.

title: I Kings 1:24
text: And Nathan said, My lord, O king, have you said, Adonijah shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne?

title: I Kings 1:25
text: For he has gone down this day, and has killed a great many of oxen and fat cattle and sheep, and has called all the king's sons and the commanders of the army, and Abiathar the priest. And behold, they eat and drink before him, and say, Let king Adonijah live.

title: I Kings 1:26
text: But he has not called me, your servant, and Zadok the priest, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and your servant Solomon.

title: I Kings 1:27
text: Is this thing done by my lord the king, and have you not shown your servant who should sit on the throne of my lord the king after him?

title: I Kings 1:28
text: And David answered and said, Call Bathsheba. And she came into the king's presence, and stood before the king.

title: I Kings 1:29
text: And the king swore, and said, [As] the LORD lives, who has redeemed my soul out of all distress,

title: I Kings 1:30
text: surely as I swore to you by the LORD God of Israel, saying, Surely Solomon your son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne in my place, even so I will do today.

title: I Kings 1:31
text: And Bathsheba bowed [her] face [to] the earth, even kneeling to the king, and said, Let my lord king David live forever.

title: I Kings 1:32
text: And king David said, Call Zadok the priest to me, and Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada. And they came before the king.

title: I Kings 1:33
text: The king also said to them, Take with you the servants of your lord, and cause Solomon my son to ride on my own mule, and bring him down to Gihon.

title: I Kings 1:34
text: And let Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anoint him king over Israel there. And blow with the ram's horn, and say, Let king Solomon live.

title: I Kings 1:35
text: And you shall come up after him, and let him come and sit upon my throne. For he shall reign in my place. And I have appointed him to be ruler over Israel and over Judah.

title: I Kings 1:36
text: And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada answered the king, and said, amen. May the LORD God of my lord the king say so.

title: I Kings 1:37
text: As the LORD has been with my lord the king, even so may He be with Solomon, and make his throne greater than the throne of my lord king David.

title: I Kings 1:38
text: And Zadok the priest, and Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites, went down and caused Solomon to ride upon king David's mule, and brought him to Gihon.

title: I Kings 1:39
text: And Zadok the priest took a horn of oil out of the Tabernacle and anointed Solomon. And they blew the ram's horn, and all the people said, Let king Solomon live!

title: I Kings 1:40
text: And all the people came up after him, and the people piped with pipes, and rejoiced [with] great joy, so that the earth was torn with their sound.

title: I Kings 1:41
text: And Adonijah heard, and all the invited guests with him. And they stopped eating. And Joab heard the sound of the ram's horn, and said, What is this noise roaring from the city?

title: I Kings 1:42
text: And he was still speaking, and behold, Jonathan the son of Abiathar the priest came. And Adonijah said to him, Come in, for you [are] a mighty man and you bring good news.

title: I Kings 1:43
text: And Jonathan answered and said to Adonijah, Truly our lord king David has made Solomon king.

title: I Kings 1:44
text: And the king has sent with him Zadok the priest, and Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites, and the Pelethites, and they have caused him to ride upon the king's mule.

title: I Kings 1:45
text: And Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet have anointed him king in Gihon. And they have come up from there rejoicing, so that the city is roaring. This [is] the noise that you heard.

title: I Kings 1:46
text: And also Solomon sits on the throne of the kingdom.

title: I Kings 1:47
text: And also the king's servants came to bless our lord king David, saying, May God make the name of Solomon better than your name, and make his throne greater than your throne. And the king bowed himself upon the bed.

title: I Kings 1:48
text: And also the king said, Blessed [is] the LORD God of Israel, who has given one to sit on my throne today, my eyes even seeing [it].

title: I Kings 1:49
text: And all those who were invited by Adonijah trembled and arose and left, each to his way.

title: I Kings 1:50
text: And Adonijah feared because of Solomon, and arose and went and caught hold on the horns of the altar.

title: I Kings 1:51
text: And it was told to Solomon, saying, Behold, Adonijah fears king Solomon. For, lo, he has caught hold on the horns of the altar, saying, Let king Solomon swear to me today that he will not kill his servant with the sword.

title: I Kings 1:52
text: And Solomon said, If he becomes a son of virtue, not a hair of his head shall fall to the earth. But if wickedness shall be found in him, then he shall die.

title: I Kings 1:53
text: And king Solomon sent, and they brought him down from the altar. And he came and bowed himself to king Solomon. And Solomon said to him, Go to your house.

title: I Kings 2:1
text: And the days of David drew near [for him] to die. And he charged Solomon his son, saying,

title: I Kings 2:2
text: I go the way of all the earth. And you be strong and show yourself a man.

title: I Kings 2:3
text: And keep the charge of the LORD your God, to walk in His ways, to keep His statutes, and His commandments, and His judgments, and His testimonies, as it is written in the law of Moses, so that you may prosper in all that you do and wherever you turn yourself,

title: I Kings 2:4
text: that the LORD may continue His word which He spoke concerning me, saying, If your sons take heed to their way, to walk before Me in truth with all their heart and with all their soul saying, there shall not be a man of yours cut off from the throne of Israel.

title: I Kings 2:5
text: And also you know what Joab the son of Zeruiah did to me, what he did to the two commanders of the armies of Israel, to Abner the son of Ner, and to Amasa the son of Jether, that he murdered them, and shed the blood of war in peace, and put the blood of war upon his girdle on his loins, and in his shoes on his feet.

title: I Kings 2:6
text: And you shall do according to your wisdom and shall not let his gray head go down to the grave in peace.

title: I Kings 2:7
text: But show kindness to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite, and let them be of those that eat at your table. For so they came to me when I fled because of Absalom your brother.

title: I Kings 2:8
text: And, behold, with you [is] Shimei the son of Gera, a Benjamite of Bahurim, who cursed me [with] a grievous curse in the day when I went to Mahanaim. But he came down to meet me at Jordan, and I swore to him by the LORD, saying, I will not put you to death with the sword.

title: I Kings 2:9
text: And now, do not hold him guiltless. For you [are] a wise man, and you know what you ought to do to him. But bring his gray head down to the grave with blood.

title: I Kings 2:10
text: And David slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David.

title: I Kings 2:11
text: And the days that David reigned over Israel [were] forty years. He reigned seven years in Hebron, and he reigned thirty-three years in Jerusalem.

title: I Kings 2:12
text: And Solomon sat upon the throne of David his father. And his kingdom was firmly established.

title: I Kings 2:13
text: And Adonijah the son of Haggith came to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon. And she said, Do you come peacefully? And he said, Peace.

title: I Kings 2:14
text: And he said, [I have] a word [to say] to you. And she said, Speak.

title: I Kings 2:15
text: And he said, You know that the kingdom was mine, and that all Israel set their faces on me that I should reign. However, the kingdom is turned around, and has become my brother's. For it was his from the LORD.

title: I Kings 2:16
text: And now I ask one favor of you; do not turn away your face. And she said to him, Speak.

title: I Kings 2:17
text: And he said, Please speak to Solomon the king, for he will not turn away your face, that he give me Abishag the Shunammite for my wife.

title: I Kings 2:18
text: And Bathsheba said, [Very] well; I will speak for you to the king.

title: I Kings 2:19
text: And Bathsheba came in to king Solomon to speak to him for Adonijah. And the king rose up to meet her, and bowed himself to her, and sat on his throne, and caused a throne to be set for the king's mother. And she sat on his right hand.

title: I Kings 2:20
text: And she said, I desire one small favor of you. Do not turn away my face. And the king said to her, Ask on, my mother, for I will not turn away your face.

title: I Kings 2:21
text: And she said, Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to your brother Adonijah for a wife.

title: I Kings 2:22
text: And king Solomon answered and said to his mother, And why do you ask Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? Ask the kingdom also for him. For he [is] my older brother! Even for him, and for Abiathar the priest, and for Joab the son of Zeruiah!

title: I Kings 2:23
text: And king Solomon swore by the LORD, saying, May God do so to me, and more He shall do, if Adonijah has not spoken this word against his life.

title: I Kings 2:24
text: And now, [as] the LORD lives, who has established me and set me on the throne of David my father, and who has made me a house, as He spoke, Adonijah shall be put to death today.

title: I Kings 2:25
text: And king Solomon sent by the hand of Benaiah the son of Jehoiada. And he fell on him so that he died.

title: I Kings 2:26
text: And the king said to Abiathar the priest, Go to Anathoth, to your fields, for you [are] worthy of death. But I will not put you to death at this time, because you carried the ark of the Lord God before David my father, and because you have been afflicted in all [that in which] my father was afflicted.

title: I Kings 2:27
text: And Solomon thrust out Abiathar from being priest to the LORD, so that he might fulfil the word of the LORD which He spoke concerning the house of Eli in Shiloh.

title: I Kings 2:28
text: And the report came to Joab. For Joab had turned after Adonijah, though he did not turn after Absalom. And Joab fled to the tabernacle of the LORD, and caught hold on the horns of the altar.

title: I Kings 2:29
text: And it was told king Solomon that Joab had fled to the tabernacle of the LORD, and, behold, [he is] by the altar. And Solomon sent Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, saying, Go fall on him.

title: I Kings 2:30
text: And Benaiah came to the tabernacle of the LORD, and said to him, So says the king, come forth! And he said, No, but I will die here. And Benaiah brought the king word again, saying, Thus said Joab, and so he answered me.

title: I Kings 2:31
text: And the king said to him, Do as he has said, and fall on him, and bury him, so that you may take away the innocent blood which Joab shed, from me and from the house of my father.

title: I Kings 2:32
text: And the LORD shall return his blood on his own head, who fell on two men more righteous and better than he, and killed them with the sword, and my father David not knowing [of it], Abner the son of Ner, commander of the army of Israel, and Amasa the son of Jether, commander of the army of Judah.

title: I Kings 2:33
text: Yea, He shall turn back their blood on the head of Joab, and on the head of his seed forever. But on David, and on his seed, and on his house, and on his throne, there shall be peace forever from the LORD.

title: I Kings 2:34
text: And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada went up and fell on him and killed him. And he was buried in his own house in the wilderness.

title: I Kings 2:35
text: And the king put Benaiah the son of Jehoiada over the army in his place. And the king put Zadok the priest in the place of Abiathar.

title: I Kings 2:36
text: And the king sent and called for Shimei, and said to him, Build a house at Jerusalem and live there, and do not go forth from there anywhere.

title: I Kings 2:37
text: For it shall be, on the day you go out and pass over the Kidron, you shall know for certain that you shall surely die. Your blood shall be on your own head.

title: I Kings 2:38
text: And Shimei said to the king, Your saying [is] good. As my lord the king has said, so will your servant do. And Shimei lived in Jerusalem many days.

title: I Kings 2:39
